chunks.heading: Pay Attention To The Notes
chunks.content:
Different fragrances are better suited for different seasons because of the natural affinity of the ingredients used to create their aroma. By choosing a fragrance that is appropriate for the season, you can ensure that you feel and smell your best no matter what the weather is like.

- Spring: During the spring, opt for lighter, fresher scents with notes of citrus or floral. These types of fragrances can help you feel energised and rejuvenated as the weather starts to warm up.

- Summer: For the hot, humid months of summer, go for a light, aquatic scent. These types of perfumes have a cool, refreshing vibe that can help you feel cool and collected, even on the hottest days.

- Autumn: As the weather starts to cool down in the autumn, choose a warmer, spicier scent. Fragrances with notes of cinnamon or clove can help you feel cozy and comfortable as the leaves start to change.

- Winter: During the colder months, opt for a rich, comforting fragrance with notes of vanilla or amber. These types of scents can help you feel warm and cozy as you brave the chilly weather.

A perfume's scent is made up of different notes, including top, middle, and base notes. The top notes are the first thing you smell when you spray the perfume and tend to be lighter and fresher. The middle or "heart" notes are the main body of the scent and emerge after the top notes have evaporated. The base notes are the deepest and longest-lasting notes and help to anchor the fragrance. Pay attention to the notes of a perfume to get an idea of its overall scent.

chunks.heading: IN SHORT…
chunks.content:
Don't be afraid to try out a few different perfumes to see which one you like best. You can either spray a small amount on your wrist and wait a few minutes to see how it develops, or you can use a perfume blotter, which is a small strip of paper that you can use to test out a fragrance.

Ultimately, the most important thing is to choose a perfume that you like and that makes you feel confident. Don't be swayed by celebrity endorsements or trend-based fragrances – choose a scent that feels like it was made just for you.

You may be looking to buy a perfume for yourself or gift it to someone else, this checklist will help you make the right choice in both the cases. Just remember, individual preferences in scents are as diverse as your taste buds, so there’s no one aroma fits all. Once you are more confident making this decision, you can understand a perfume by just reading its notes online. Happy shopping!

chunks.heading: Who are you buying it for?
chunks.content:
When it comes to buying perfumes, it can be challenging to determine which scent is the right one for you or the one you’re buying it for. With so many options available, it's essential to know how to test perfumes properly before making a purchase. There are two ways to go about choosing the right one. One, making a choice physically when you have access to the product; and two, selecting one online on the basis of all the information available to you on the website/listing. In this article we’ll be delving deep into the second category. So, let’s start…

CHOOSING A PERFUME ONLINE

Interestingly, choosing a perfume online can be a tricky task, as you can’t test the scent in person, but it can also be a great way to find unique and hard-to-find fragrances. Online retailers often have a wider selection than brick and mortar stores, and you can easily compare prices and read reviews from other customers. Additionally, buying online can be more convenient and save time. With a bit of research and some careful consideration, buying Perfume Online can be a great way to find the perfect scent at a great price.

Before we get into the aromatic details, the primary differentiation in perfumes is marked by who it is for: men, women and unisex fragrances. It’s important to note this because a lot of times certain types of ingredients are associated with a specific gender but its combination with other ingredients may make it behave absolutely differently.

For instance, floral fragrances are characterised by scents that are typically associated with feminine, flower-like aromas. But don’t be trapped in this word because not everything that is floral is feminine. Look at the other ingredients too before making a choice. Some of men’s favourite choices often feature some iconic flowers like lavender, neroli and patchouli.

chunks.heading: What’s The Occasion
chunks.content:
If you already know this, it will be easier for you to pick a fragrance for him. But usually perfumes are very subjective and personal, so even if you know someone well, making a custom-fit choice for someone may be expecting too much of yourself. But the good news is that there are few categories that majority of the men tend to show an affinity towards.

Oriental fragrances (also called spicy fragrances) that have a warm and spicy scent, often with notes of vanilla, amber, or musk.

Fresh fragrances that are characterised by their light, crisp, and clean scents

Woody fragrances have a more robust and earthy scent, often with notes of cedar, sandalwood, or patchouli.

Next, take into account the occasion and the time of day they usually like to wear their fragrances. Some people strictly wear perfumes on dressy occasions, while some others are more serious about always smelling good.

Some fragrances are more suitable for formal occasions, while others are better for casual wear. Additionally, some scents are more appropriate for daytime wear, while others are better for nighttime. If you feel they’re more experimental with how they smell and don’t have a very strict routine with perfumes, you can give them a perfumes combo kit, with multiple options to go with for different occasions and time of the day.

Read the reviews and check the ingredient list. The fragrance pyramid is often provided on perfume's website, it is a list of ingredients that show the olfactive notes created by the ingredients used in the fragrance, this will give you an idea of the dominant notes and how they might smell together. Additionally, reading reviews from other customers can also provide insight into how a fragrance smells and performs on different people.

- Make sure you’re buying it from an authentic retailer online.

[BONUS]

WHEN YOU HAVE PHYSICAL ACCESS TO THE PERFUME

First, it's important to understand that perfumes react differently with different body chemistry. What may smell great on one person may not have the same effect on another. When a fragrance is applied to the skin, it will be absorbed by the body and interact with the oils present on the skin. Additionally, the warmth of the skin can also cause the fragrance to evolve over time and release different notes than it would when smelled on paper. So, it's best to test perfumes on your own skin rather than on a piece of paper or card.

chunks.heading: IN SHORT...
chunks.content:
When testing perfumes, it's essential to give the scent time to settle and develop on your skin, because fragrances are composed of different notes or layers, which evolve over time. When a fragrance is first applied, the top notes (which are the most volatile and evaporate quickly) will be the most prominent. As the fragrance dries down, the middle (or heart) notes will become more apparent, and finally the base notes will come out.

Spray or dab a small amount of the fragrance on your wrist or the inside of your elbow and wait for about 15 minutes. This will give you a better idea of how the scent will evolve over time and how it will interact with your body chemistry.

It's not a good idea to test more than two or three perfumes at a time. The sense of smell can become overwhelmed by too many scents, making it difficult to distinguish between them. Also, it can be challenging to keep track of which fragrance is which, and which one you liked or didn't like. It's easy to become confused and to mix up the fragrances, which can lead to making a wrong decision. On the other hand, testing a small number of fragrances will allow you to focus on the nuances of each scent and make a more informed decision.

Lastly, it's crucial to pay attention to how the fragrance makes you feel. A perfume should not only smell good but also make you feel good. So, pay attention to how the scent makes you feel emotionally, as this is an important aspect of the fragrance experience. You don’t want to be stuck with something for the rest of the day that feels like unwanted baggage.

blogs.title: How to find your signature scent?

chunks.heading: 1. Reflect On Yourself To Discover Your Scent
chunks.content:
Finding a signature scent is not just a treasure hunt; it’s a personal journey where certain fragrances evoke memories you hold on to, emotions you feel, and nostalgic whispers of the past. So, your signature scent should be as unique as your moments and experiences, reflecting your authentic self.

This process of finding your signature scent will be exhilarating and introspective - an invitation to uncover the scents that resonate with your essence.

Before diving into the scent-ional world of scents, treat each fragrance as a reflection of your life experiences. Some will be light and fleeting, like brief encounters, while others will be strong and long-lasting. Don’t forget to engage all your senses; let the fragrances dance on your skin and mingle with your memories.

Take a moment to recall a fragrance you are closely associated with. Was it the comforting aroma of your mother, the fresh smell of rain-soaked earth, or the sweet fragrance of cookies baking in the oven?

It could be connected to memorable moments in your life - your wedding day, graduation, or a special trip. For instance, if a particular scent reminds you of your honeymoon in the hills, it might be worth exploring similar fragrances that capture that essence.

You may also delve into your everyday comforts. This could be the refreshing smell of fresh linen, the rich aroma of brewing coffee, or even the fresh scent of morning air. These familiar scents can guide you toward fragrances that evoke feelings of warmth and security.

chunks.heading: 2. Explore Different Fragrance Families
chunks.content:
Fragrances are about diverse combinations and olfactory notes, each evoking different emotions and memories. To simplify this universe of possibilities, there are four main fragrance families:

1. Florals: The most common family, offering romantic, delicate, and feminine notes that smell like freshly cut flowers or powdery essences. They can evoke feelings of joy and nostalgia, making them perfect for those who cherish romantic memories.

If you’re one of them, then try rose-based perfume for something romantic and elegant. You can prefer Jasmine if you like a trickier and more masculine fragrance, while for the most classic with floral and minty essence, Lavender is right for you. For something different, explore scents with Osmanthus, Champaca, Iris, or Neroli and Orange Blossom notes.

2. Ambers: Previously known as the oriental, these scents combine herbs, spices, and dry powdery resin. They create a comforting, sensual, and exotic aura with spicy and warm notes of ginger, cinnamon, and vanilla - perfect for those who wish to make a bold statement.

If you love the depth of cedar, sandalwood, or musk, an amber scent with woody notes might be your match.

3. Woods: As the name suggests, this family features earthy, masculine, earthy, and grounding notes. The blend of sandalwood, patchouli, and dry notes evokes warmth and coziness - ideal for someone who finds comfort in nature.

If you resonate with earthy and woody characteristics, try scents with cedarwood, sandalwood, pine, oud, and patchouli.

4. Fresh: This family offers zesty, aromatic fragrances often with woodsy undertones. These scents instantly make you feel refreshed and rejuvenated with the light, bright, sparkling, and natural aromas of lemon, bergamot, orange, and grapefruit - uplifting your spirits and perfect for daytime wear.

Approach this exploration with an open mind - sometimes, the scents we least expect to love can surprise us. Once you choose your fragrance family, find complementing notes that best suit your selected scent profile.

chunks.heading: 4. The Right Way To Test The Perfumes
chunks.content:
Perfumes, like music, have fragrance notes: Top, Middle, and Base. These notes harmonize to create a complete fragrance and decide how the scent will unfold.

Top Notes: The first you smell when you apply any perfume - setting the initial mood and tone of the fragrance. These are fresher and the most prominent notes such as lemon, bergamot, orange, pine, and lavender, usually lasting around 30 minutes.

Middle Notes: Once the top note fades, these “heart notes” hold the essence of the perfume. They are like bridges between the initial impression and the final dry-down. Rose, jasmine, lily of the valley, and clove are the most popular middle notes, lasting for hours.

Base Notes: These are the most remembered notes as they are the slowest to evaporate. They provide longevity and set the foundation of the fragrance with their rich, warm, and sensual characteristics contributing to the fragrance’s overall sillage and staying power. Amber, musk, vanilla, sandalwood, patchouli, and cedarwood are popular base notes, often lasting for hours or even days.

When testing fragrances, applying them directly to your skin is crucial because body chemistry plays a significant role in how a fragrance develops over time. Here’s how to test scents effectively:

- Spray a small amount on your wrist or inner elbow, rather than using paper testers. This allows you to experience how the fragrance interacts with your skin's natural oils.

- Give the fragrance time to settle - at least several hours. Pay attention to how it evolves from top notes (the initial scent) to heart notes (the core scent) and finally base notes (the lasting scent). This progression helps you to understand how the fragrance will wear throughout the day.

- Limit testing two or three scents at a time to prevent olfactory fatigue. Trying too many at once can make it difficult to distinguish between them.

Pro Tip: If possible, maintain a journal as you explore different fragrances to document your experience and their development over time.

chunks.heading: You’re All Set To Get Your Signature Scent
chunks.content:
Sometimes those closest to us can provide insights we might overlook. Once you've narrowed down your favorites, share them with friends or family members whose opinions you trust. They might recall specific memories associated with certain scents that resonate with them. Ask how each fragrance makes them feel or what memories it evokes when they smell it on you. Their feedback could reinforce or challenge your perceptions.

Once you've found a fragrance that resonates emotionally and evokes cherished memories, embrace it as part of your identity - it should feel like an extension of who you are. Your signature scent will leave an aromatic trail wherever you go, becoming synonymous with your presence.

Finding your signature scent is not just about choosing a fragrance; it's about discovering a piece of yourself that resonates deeply within - a beautiful reminder that every moment can be captured in a scent, creating an everlasting connection between who you are today and who you've always been.

blogs.title: Why You Still Smell Bad By Noon (And How to Actually Fix It)

chunks.heading: The Science Most Brands Don't Explain
chunks.content:
You spray deodorant every morning without thinking twice. But here's what most guys don't realize: that cloud of fragrance you're blasting under your arms isn't actually stopping sweat. It's masking what happens after sweat meets bacteria—which is the real source of body odor.

Understanding how deodorants work (versus how you think they work) changes everything. It affects which product you buy, how you apply it, and whether you smell fresh at 6 PM or need to sneak off for emergency reapplication.

At Bombay Shaving Company, we've developed deodorants specifically engineered for Indian conditions—humidity that makes you sweat through your shirt by 10 AM, pollution that clings to skin, and temperatures that swing from freezing AC to outdoor heat within minutes. These aren't international formulas adapted for India. They're built from scratch for how Indian men actually live.

Sweat Itself Doesn't Smell:

Your body produces sweat to regulate temperature. Fresh sweat is mostly water and salt—completely odorless. The smell comes when bacteria on your skin break down sweat proteins. That characteristic "BO" everyone dreads? That's bacterial waste products, not sweat itself.

Deodorant vs. Antiperspirant:

Deodorants neutralize odor-causing bacteria and mask smell with fragrance. Antiperspirants physically block sweat glands using aluminum compounds—literally preventing sweat from reaching your skin surface. Most products marketed as "deos" are actually deodorant-antiperspirant hybrids.

The Indian Climate Factor:

International deo formulas assume moderate temperatures and lower humidity. Indian summers hit 45°C with 70%+ humidity in many cities. Your body produces more sweat, bacteria multiply faster, and fragrances evaporate quicker. Standard formulas simply don't hold up.

chunks.heading: Our Spray Deodorant Collection
chunks.content:
Spray Deodorants (The Coverage Kings):

Sprays disperse fragrance and active ingredients over larger areas quickly. They dry almost instantly, so you can dress immediately without that sticky wait. The alcohol base kills bacteria effectively while helping fragrance project further.

Perfect for rushed mornings, post-gym quick changes, and guys who hate the feeling of product on skin. The wide coverage means you're not missing patches—a common problem with roll-ons when you're rushing.

Roll-On Deodorant (The Precision Specialist):

Roll-ons apply concentrated product directly where you need it. No wasted spray in the air, no accidental inhaling, no product on bathroom walls. The direct application means active ingredients stay in contact with skin longer, providing extended protection.

Our Roll-On Deo does something most sprays can't: it contains AHA/BHA exfoliators (Lactic acid, Glycolic acid, Salicylic acid) that gradually fade dark underarms while controlling odor. That discoloration from years of shaving and product buildup? This addresses it.

Alcohol-free, gas-free, aluminum-free, and paraben-free formula means even sensitive skin tolerates it well. Quick-absorbing with zero residue—no white marks on your black shirt. The refreshing aqua fragrance works for daily wear without overwhelming elevators or meeting rooms.

Red Spice (150ml):

This is your hot and humid weather warrior. When Mumbai monsoons hit or Delhi summer peaks, Red Spice holds the line. Strong scent means it projects confidence without constant reapplication.

The spice notes cut through heat-induced sweat better than fresh or citrus fragrances that fade fast in humidity. Built specifically for Indian weather conditions that destroy international deo performance.

Best for: Outdoor jobs, construction work, sales roles involving travel, gym sessions, anyone who sweats heavily and needs serious staying power.

Black Vibe (150ml):

Complexity in a can. Opens with roses and jasmine—unexpected florals that feel masculine, not feminine. Quickly transitions into Agarwood (Oud), adding that deep, expensive depth typically reserved for high-end perfumes. Settles into musky, woody base notes that linger hours after application.

This isn't your gym deo. Black Vibe is for evening plans, dates, parties, occasions where you want people asking what you're wearing. Sensual without being aggressive, mature without feeling old.

The fragrance profile works well layered under cologne or worn alone. Sophisticated enough for formal events, bold enough for nightlife.

Best for: Evening wear, special occasions, guys who appreciate complex fragrances, layering with other scents.

Noir (150ml):

Mystery meets practicality. Woody notes provide depth and warmth, while citrus keeps it fresh and approachable. That balance makes Noir incredibly versatile—works for office, casual hangouts, or evening plans without feeling wrong in any setting.

Controls body odor effectively even for guys with heavy sweat issues. The citrusy notes specifically combat that sour smell active sweat produces. Long-lasting performance means morning application carries through to evening.

Raw, sensual vibe perfect for guys who prefer understated confidence over loud statements. Doesn't announce your arrival but definitely gets noticed up close.

Best for: All-day wear, office environments, guys with active sweat concerns, anyone wanting versatility in one bottle.

chunks.heading: Matching Deo to Your Day
chunks.content:
Applying to Wet Skin:

Deodorant needs dry skin to work properly. Wet skin dilutes the formula, reducing effectiveness. Post-shower, wait 2-3 minutes until underarms are completely dry before applying.

Spraying Too Close:

Hold spray deos 6-8 inches away. Too close concentrates product in small areas, causing white marks and wasting half the can. Proper distance distributes evenly.

Skipping After Shaving:

Shaving creates micro-cuts. Applying alcohol-based products immediately causes burning and irritation. Either shave at night (apply deo next morning) or wait 10-15 minutes after morning shaving.

Not Shaking Spray Cans:

Ingredients settle. Not shaking means inconsistent performance—strong some days, weak others. Five good shakes before each use ensures proper mixing.

Over-Application:

More doesn't mean better protection. Two seconds per underarm for sprays, four rolls up-down for roll-ons. Excess product clumps, stains clothes, and wastes money.

Applying Only in Morning:

If you shower twice daily (common in Indian heat), reapply after evening shower. Washing removes morning protection—leaving you unguarded for evening plans.

Workout Days:

Roll-On Deo specifically mentions gym use, marathons, and active lifestyles. The quick-absorbing, residue-free formula won't mix with sweat to create that gross paste under your arms. No stains on your athletic wear.

Office Environments:

Noir's balanced citrus-woody profile won't overpower closed spaces. Professional without being boring, noticeable without being aggressive. Works in AC-controlled environments where strong scents amplify awkwardly.

Hot, Humid Weather:

Red Spice is literally formulated for this. When temperature and humidity both hit high numbers, standard deos surrender. This one fights through.

Evening Events:

Black Vibe's complexity suits occasions where first impressions matter. The Oud-based depth projects sophistication. Perfect for dates, parties, weddings, networking events.

Sensitive Skin Days:

Roll-On Deo's alcohol-free, gas-free, aluminum-free formula minimizes irritation. Gentle enough for reactive skin while maintaining protection.

chunks.heading: Why Indian-Formulated Matters
chunks.content:
Years of shaving, deodorant buildup, and friction darken underarm skin. Most guys just accept it. Our R oll-On Deo actively addresses this with AHA/BHA exfoliators.

Lactic acid and Glycolic acid gently remove dead skin cells and buildup. Salicylic acid penetrates pores, clearing congestion. Over weeks of consistent use, discoloration visibly fades.

This matters more than you think. Lighter underarms mean more confidence going sleeveless, better comfort in tank tops, and eliminating that self-conscious feeling at pools or beaches.

The Two-Product System:

Roll-On for regular days—work, errands, casual plans. Spray for high-intensity days—gym, outdoor work, special events. This approach maximizes benefits of both formats.

Seasonal Rotation:

Summer demands stronger formulas like Red Spice. Winter allows lighter options like Noir. Matching intensity to conditions improves comfort and effectiveness.

Layering with Cologne:

If you wear cologne, choose complementary deo scents. Woody colognes pair with Noir or Black Vibe. Fresh, aquatic colognes work with Roll-On's aqua fragrance. Avoid competing scents that create confusing fragrance profiles.

Emergency Backup:

Keep travel-size or spare deo in gym bag, car, or office drawer. Unexpected meetings, spontaneous plans, or just longer-than-expected days happen. Having backup prevents stress and maintains confidence.

Climate Testing:

Our formulas are tested in actual Indian conditions—45°C heat, monsoon humidity, pollution exposure. International brands test in controlled environments that don't match real-world Indian use.

Skin Type Consideration:

Indian skin types differ from Western and East Asian populations. Our formulations account for these differences in sebum production, sensitivity patterns, and product absorption.

Value Pricing:

₹2.37 per ml means quality protection without luxury markups. You're not subsidizing international shipping, import duties, or brand celebrity endorsements. Just effective deodorants priced fairly.

chunks.heading: Frequently Asked Questions
chunks.content:
Most guys blame the product when protection fails. Usually it's application timing or technique.

Apply to completely dry, clean skin. Give it 60 seconds to dry before dressing. Don't overapply. Reapply after showering if you shower multiple times daily.

Choose the right formula for your activity level and environment. Heavy sweater in summer? Red Spice. Office worker with sensitive skin? Roll-On. Evening event? Black Vibe.

Store properly—cool, dry place away from direct heat. Extreme temperatures damage formula effectiveness.

Can I use deodorant on other body parts?

Technically yes, but unnecessary. Underarms have the highest concentration of apocrine sweat glands (the ones producing odor). Other areas don't need it.

Why do I still sweat after applying?

Most deodorants aren't antiperspirants. They control odor, not sweat production. Sweating is normal and healthy. The goal is sweat without smell.

Can women use these products?

Absolutely. Marketing might target men, but formulas work for anyone. Fragrance preference is personal, not gendered.

How long does one bottle last?

150ml spray with proper use (2 seconds per pit, twice daily) lasts roughly 30-40 days. Roll-on with correct application (4 swipes per pit, twice daily) extends slightly longer.

Is aluminum in deodorants dangerous?

Research shows no conclusive link between aluminum in antiperspirants and health issues. However, our Roll-On is aluminum-free for those preferring to avoid it anyway.

Can I apply deo before working out?

Yes, but apply 2-3 minutes before exercise so it dries completely. Wet application won't protect as effectively.

Why does my deo stop working after weeks of use?

Your nose adapts to constant fragrance exposure—you stop noticing it. Others still smell it. If genuinely concerned, switch fragrances monthly to reset.

Do I need to reapply after sweating heavily?

If you showered or thoroughly washed underarms, yes. If just sweated without washing, the formula should still be working.

chunks.heading: Beyond Just Smelling Good
chunks.content:
Confidence correlates directly with feeling fresh. That subtle anxiety about whether you smell okay affects performance in meetings, interactions on dates, comfort in social situations.

Effective deodorant eliminates that background stress. You stop worrying about raising your arms or standing too close to someone. Small thing, massive impact.

The right deo isn't luxury—it's basic respect for yourself and people around you. At ₹356 for 150ml or similar accessible pricing, there's genuinely no excuse for skipping it.

Choose your formula based on actual needs, not packaging. Apply it correctly. Stop overthinking. Body odor is a solved problem—you just have to use the solution consistently.

blogs.title: Winter Fragrances For Men: A Quick Guide

chunks.content:
Winter is a great time to switch up your Fragrance game. The colder months call for scents that are warm, rich, and invigorating, and there are many great options for men to choose from. In this short guide, we'll be exploring some of the best winter fragrances for men, as well as how to choose the right fragrance for you.

One of the key things to consider when choosing a winter fragrance is the type of scent you prefer. Some men prefer fresh, crisp scents that remind them of the outdoors, while others prefer warmer, more spicy or woody scents. When choosing a winter fragrance, it's also important to consider the strength and longevity of the scent. You want a fragrance that will last throughout the day, but not be too overpowering. Eau de parfum and eau de toilette are both good options for winter fragrances, as they are strong enough to last all day, but not so strong that they will be overwhelming.

Things to consider before buying a perfume for winters:

- Scent: Winter fragrances tend to be more complex and rich than those for other seasons. Look for fragrances with notes of spices, woods and other warm, comforting scents.

- Longevity: winter fragrances should have good lasting power, as you don’t want to have to reapply your perfume too frequently in the cold weather.

- Occasion: Consider the occasion for which you will be wearing the fragrance. A more formal event may call for a more elegant, sophisticated scent, while a casual gathering might be better suited to a more laid-back fragrance.

- Personal preference: Ultimately, the most popular factor in choosing a winter perfume is your own personal preference. Choose a scent that you love and that makes you feel confident and comfortable.

chunks.heading: IN SHORT…
chunks.content:
Woody. Intimate.

A delicate blend of captivating woody notes and fresh blast of citrus.

Vanilla. Vice.

The alluring aroma of rich Vanilla mixed with the spicy sass of Cardamom, Nutmeg and fresh Neroli

Dark. Spicy.

A new world of fantasies with intricate spices blending into rich woody notes.

Morning. Fresh

A radical cocktail of zesty lemon, sensual floral scents and earthy sandalwood

Make sure that you go through the top, middle and bottom notes of any perfume that you buy. The real secret of smelling great lies in the arrangement of these olfactive notes. So go ahead, spritz with confidence and may you smell great all year long!

blogs.title: 5 Habits That Are Destroying Your Grooming Tools

chunks.heading: 2. Putting the cap back on while it’s wet
chunks.content:
Ever found yourself wondering why your trimmer and razor don’t last long enough? Even when you spend a good amount of money on them, they still turn dull, rough, or dead well before their time.

The problem might not be your product, but how you take care of it.

Whether it’s the way you charge your trimmer or the way you leave your razor clogged with hair, there are plenty of post-trim and post-shave habits that silently ruin the efficiency of your grooming tools.

Let’s shed some light on these habits and what you can do to avoid them.

Dull or poorly maintained grooming tools don’t just perform badly. They affect your skin.

A dull blade requires more pressure. More pressure increases the risk of micro-cuts. Micro-cuts can lead to irritation, razor burn, and ingrown hairs.

So this isn’t just about protecting metal. It’s about protecting your face.

It feels convenient. You shave. You rinse. You place it next to your soap and face wash.

Big mistake.

Showers create constant humidity and steam. Even when the water isn’t running, the environment stays damp. Metal + moisture + oxygen = oxidation. That’s rust.

Prolonged exposure to moisture accelerates blade dullness and weakens the edge. Humidity can also affect lubricating strips.

Do this instead:

- Rinse your razor thoroughly.

- Shake off excess water.

- Pat it dry with a clean towel.

- Store it outside the shower area in a dry, ventilated spot.

Bonus points for thinking about protecting your razor after shaving.

But protection without thought can end up doing more harm than good.

Putting the cap on your razor while it’s still wet traps moisture inside. This can cause corrosion and bacterial growth.

Over time, this leads to:

- Faster dulling

- Mineral buildup

- Slight tugging while shaving

Tugging means friction, and friction means irritation.

Do this instead:

Only cap your razor once it’s fully dry. If you’re in a rush, leave it uncapped in a dry area and cap it later.

chunks.heading: 4. Letting hair build up inside the blade
chunks.content:
This one is more common than you’d think.

Many men struggle with trimmers that stop performing well and don’t realise the solution has been in their trimmer box all along.

Most trimmers use stainless steel blades. When two metal blades move against each other at high speed, they create friction. Friction creates heat. Heat increases wear.

That’s why many trimmers come with blade oil.

Oiling your trimmer regularly reduces blade friction, prevents rust, and maintains smooth cutting.

Skipping oil won’t destroy your trimmer overnight. But it slowly reduces performance. You may notice uneven cutting, slight pulling, or the need for more passes. That’s blade wear talking.

Do this instead:

Apply 1–2 drops of trimmer blade oil across the blades after cleaning and drying them. Turn the trimmer on for a few seconds to distribute the oil evenly. Wipe off the excess.

It takes less than a minute and can significantly extend blade life.

You rinse your trimmer. Good. But do you remove the attachment and clean underneath?

Loose hair can accumulate over time inside the head and beneath the attachments.

This can lead to:

- Reduced efficiency

- Increased blade friction

- Moisture retention

In some cases, compacted hair can even slightly misalign blade components. That’s when you feel uneven cutting or hear unusual sounds coming from your trimmer.

And if the buildup stays damp, it can also lead to bacterial growth, especially in humid climates.

Do this instead:

Don’t just rinse your trimmer while the blade is still attached. Remove detachable heads and brush out the hair first. Then clean the attachment properly and ensure there’s no stray hair or water in either the attachment or the body.

chunks.heading: In conclusion
chunks.content:
This feels convenient. Anything that foams up must be cleaning your tools, right?

But most body washes contain:

- Heavy fragrance compounds

- Oils

- Moisturising agents

- Exfoliating particles or scrubbing beads

These ingredients can leave residue on blades and attachments. Residue attracts debris. Debris traps moisture. Moisture accelerates corrosion.

Fragranced residue can also irritate your skin if it remains on the blade.

Do this instead:

For stubborn dirt, use mild liquid soap without heavy oils or fragrances. Rinse thoroughly and dry completely.

Your grooming tools aren’t fragile. But they aren’t indestructible either.

If your razor feels rough faster than expected or your trimmer isn’t cutting like it used to, don’t blame the product immediately.

Check your habits.

Fix the environment.

Protect the blade.

Your tools will last longer. And your skin will thank you.

blogs.title: 5 Reasons Why You Should Totally Buy Your Valentine's Day Gift Early

chunks.content:
As Valentine's Day approaches many people have started planning their gifts, thanks to all the buzz around the (now major) holiday in the month of February. But most of us end up actually buying the gift for our partner pretty late. It’s not a fallacy or out of reluctance. Interestingly, a study suggests that our brain is hard-wired to procrastinate the decision of actually buying the gift, and what follows is endless research and anxiety. This is so because subconsciously we keep looking for ‘better’ options and ‘better’ deals before we finally seal the deal. But why wait until the last minute when you can buy a gift early on? Here are a few reasons why buying a Valentine's Day gift early is a good idea:

1. Avoid the rush.
Think of it this way, if you were going to a concert and you knew that the doors opened at 7pm, would you wait until 6:59pm to start lining up? Of course not! You would get there early to avoid the rush and ensure that you get a good spot. Buying gifts is no different. Buying a gift early means you can avoid the crowds and the stress that comes with last-minute shopping. Plus, you'll have more time to find the perfect gift without feeling rushed, and you won’t have to worry about not being able to find what you’re looking for.

2. Show your loved one that you care.
When you’re buying a gift early you’re not just showing your partner that you’re thinking of them, but you’re also sending them a message that you care about them, and you want to make the occasion special for them. It’s like a secret love letter hidden in a present. It also indicates that you’re invested in your relationship by putting your time, effort and money into it.

3. Give yourself time to plan a surprise.
Anticipating Valentine’s Day takes effort and preparation. Make a list of all the things you want to do and plan ahead to ensure a memorable experience for your significant other. One important aspect to consider is purchasing your gift early. This will not only ensure there are no disappointments but also give you more time to plan and execute it.

4. Show that you’re not just fulfilling a formality.
By buying a gift early, you demonstrate your thoughtfulness and effort in making the day special. It shows that you are not just going through the motions, but that you have taken the time to consider what would make your partner feel loved and appreciated. Early gift shopping allows you to take your time to choose something that truly represents your feelings, without the added pressure of a deadline. This effort and attention to detail will not go unnoticed and will make the day even more memorable.

5. It's an opportunity to show that you're excited about your relationship.
Buying a gift early for your Valentine’s Day celebration shows that you are looking forward to this special day and are eager to make it memorable for both of you. By taking the time to plan ahead and choose a thoughtful gift, you express your love and affection in a tangible way, making the day even more meaningful. This small act of love and consideration is a powerful message of your commitment and excitement for your relationship.

IN SHORT…
So, don't wait until the last minute. Just remember that the early bird gets the worm, or in this case, the perfect Valentine's Day gift. Trust us, your partner will thank you for being the ultimate Cupid-in-training. So, grab your quiver of ideas and arrows of love, and start your early gift shopping journey today! Happy Valentine's Day!

blogs.title: 8 ways to deal with body odour and sweat

chunks.heading: Major reasons behind this
chunks.content:
Hey, can you smell that?

Hey, what’s that smell?

Followed by the awkward glances and eyes looking at you. That moment feels like every eye in the world is watching you and you know how bad you smell.

If so, you are not alone in this. Every person has a unique odour, but the moment sweat comes into the picture, it is a big turn-off for everyone around.

This happens when the bacteria on your skin comes in contact with sweat, and hence the foul smell.

Covers: Scientific Reasons + Lifestyle Choices + Clothing Choices And Your Diet

Sweat: Sweat is one of the biggest drivers of body odour in your body. Your body releases sweat as a method to cool down your body. When sweat mixes with bacteria that is sitting on your skin's surface, it can result in an unpleasant odour. Your body has sweat glands and the areas with more sweat glands like the armpits and groin are more prone to body odour.

Diet: Certain food makes your sweat smell even before it comes into contact with the bacteria on your body. So things like garlic, and sulphur-containing food lead to body odour. Another interesting aspect of this is that there are people who are born with genetic metabolic disorders which prevent them from digesting certain amino acids and when the by-product of those foods gets excreted by sweat you get 'Bad Odour'.

Hygiene: Bad hygiene routines like not having a bath regularly, not cleaning armpits and groin area, and wearing the same clothes over and over again can worsen this situation. This allows the bacteria to grow on your skin and leads to a stronger body odour.

Hormonal Changes: These changes are fluctuating, especially the changes that occur during puberty and menopause, which can increase sweating and alter the composition of sweat, making your body a more favourable place for bacteria to flourish.

Stress and Anxiety: Yes emotional stress or anxiety is also on this list. They stimulate the sweat glands of your body, and all this increases the chances of odour in your body.

Alcohol and Smoking: The consumption of alcohol and smoking affects the body significantly. Alcohol makes your body sweat more, while smoking can leave a stinking odour on the skin and on your breath.

Clothing: Wearing tight or non-breathable fabric traps sweat against the skin. This creates a favourable environment for bacteria to grow and produce more body odour.

chunks.heading: Here’s how you deal with it
chunks.content:
Covers: Ways And Methods To Fix This Condition For Good

Regular Bathing: This one is painfully obvious but yeah, increase your bathing frequency if you're not frequently bathing. Go for an antibacterial soap with odour-fighting properties and pay special attention to the armpits, groin, and feet area.

Use Antiperspirant or Deodorant: Antiperspirants reduce sweating, while Deodorants mask your odour. Use it after you’re done bathing on your clean, dry skin, especially around the underarms.

Change Clothes Regularly: listen, it's not that difficult, change your clothes more frequently and if you’re planning to get new clothes go for the breathable ones. Go for more breathable fabrics like cotton or linen. The breathable fabrics help in better air circulation eventually reducing odour. Avoid tight-fitting clothes as they trap sweat and bacteria.

Maintain Good Foot Hygiene: You need to wash your feet daily. Follow a routine that involves washing feet regularly, and then drying them thoroughly. If you wish to take it to the next level sprinkle foot powder or use odour-fighting insoles.

Stay Hydrated: Drinking plenty of water helps regulate body temperature and dilute the compounds that can make sweat smell stronger. The recommendation is 3-4 litres daily. Additionally, add electrolytes to your hydration plan to consume the necessary salts your body needs. Coconut is the best source for this.

Dietary Changes: Stay away from foods that are known to increase the body odour such as garlic, onions, asparagus, and other spicy sulphur-rich foods.

Alcohol and Smoking: limit alcohol and smoking consumption, as both contribute to body odour.

Use Fragrance-Free Products: Seems counter-intuitive but hear us out. Scented lotions, perfumes, or body washes, mix with body odour and create a new surprisingly unpleasant smell. Avoid doing that.

See A Doctor: If you have a sudden drastic change in your body odour and there is no change in your habits, no new medications, or if you can't figure out why you don't smell like you used to smell, consider taking a professional opinion. A doctor will examine your situation better and they will identify the reason why you have a body odour issue.

chunks.heading: Frequently Asked Questions
chunks.content:
So, to wrap things up, when you deal with body odour, it boils down to a few things like good hygiene, diet, better lifestyle choices and a little self-awareness. Since you've read so far you know the drill - shower regularly, get an antiperspirant and wear fresh clothes with breathable fabrics.

So, stay fresh and healthy!

Q. What are the natural ways to combat body odour?

A. You can use lemon juice or alum on the areas where you feel your body produces the most odour. Incorporating these in your routine can help neutralise odour. But, make sure you do not have any nicks or cuts in those areas. Even the slightest cut will be painful if you use any of it there.

Q. Should I shower more often to prevent body odour?

A. When facing extreme body odour conditions, you should shower twice daily. Especially after a workout or sweating, to remove sweat and bacteria.

Q. Can excessive use of deodorants or antiperspirants be harmful to my health?

A. Deodorants and antiperspirants are safe, but excessive use may lead to skin irritation. The skin might act up if you have sensitive skin.

blogs.title: 6 Grooming Tips For Your First Date: Express to Impress

chunks.heading: 1. Choose A Hairstyle That Suits You
chunks.content:
First dates are like stepping into a magical world, where every moment is infused with excitement and butterflies in your stomach. It’s about meeting someone new, and making an impression that will probably stick with them for a long time. (Whatever happened to not judging a book by its cover?) As per a study, people make snap judgments within the first 7 seconds of a meeting - faster than it took you to read this far. Psyched?

For Gen Z daters, where dating apps and quick meetups are the norm, those special yet crucial first moments can make or break a potential match. But here’s the silver lining. While nothing can be done about your personality (we believe you’ll take care of that part) your grooming game can be controlled with some simple tips, and add to that crucial first impression.

Grooming is not just about looking good; it's about expressing yourself authentically and leaving a lasting impression, because when you look good, you also feel good. The individuals who spend time on personal grooming are found to portray higher confidence levels, lower pre-date anxiety, and hold better social interactions. So here’s a non-exhaustive list of 6 things that you can do to play this in your favour.

Your hair is often the first thing someone notices when they first meet you. Unless you manage a distraction with a flashy clothing (which we highly recommend you don’t). So, your hairstyle can set the tone for your date. Start with clean hair; use a shampoo and conditioner suitable for your hair type. Look for products infused with natural ingredients, like coconut oil or argan oil, that can add moisture and shine.

And then choose a style that complements your face shape and personal style. For instance, a classic crew cut or fade works well for short hair, while textured crops or side parts are versatile options for medium-length hair. If you have longer hair, consider a loose bun or ponytail for a neat look. While styling your hair, you can even use products like Hair Gel, Pomade, or Wax to avoid a greasy appearance.

Pro Tip: Avoid over-complicated hairstyles, stick to what you can manage easily.

chunks.heading: 3. Follow Skincare Routine For Clearer Skin
chunks.content:
A well groomed beard can enhance your features tremendously. Decide whether you want a clean shave or a beard. For a clean shave, use a sensitive-on-skin razor with lubra strip and naturally formulated shaving cream or foam to achieve a smooth finish, followed by aftershave essentials to soothe the skin. If you prefer to choose a beard, use a trimmer specially designed for styling the beard that lets you explore and create unlimited beard styles to keep it well-trimmed, in-shaped, and in trend.

Choose a beard style that suits your face shape. For round faces, Goatee works well as it elongates the chin. Where Full Beard complements square faces and adds masculinity. Go for Stubble if you want to enhance ruggedness without requiring extensive maintenance. You can also use grooming products such as beard oil to set and keep your beard in shape.

Pro Tip: Don’t forget to comb your beard to distribute natural oils evenly.

Healthy skin is essential for making a great first impression. Use either a deep cleansing or de-tanning face wash twice daily as per your skin type (oily, dry, combination) to pull out dirt, wash off impurities, remove tan, and fade dark spots. Followed by a face scrub, 2-3 times per week, for gentle exfoliation to remove dead skin cells and promote cell turnover, helping to achieve a smoother complexion. Apply a moisturizer infused with the ultra-hydrating power of shea butter to pamper your skin and facial area with deep moisturization and nourishment. Look for products tailored to your skin type - lightweight gels for oily skin and richer creams for dry skin.

Pro Tip: Without a doubt, wear sunscreen always to prevent skin damage and allergies.

chunks.heading: 6. Maintain Oral Care For Fresh Breath
chunks.content:
Taking care of your body goes beyond just hygiene; it’s about feeling good in your skin. Start with a refreshing shower before your date. Use a deep-cleansing body wash that leaves you feeling refreshed and sweet-smelling. Look after your sensitive areas as well like armpits, chest, and back - trim off any excess hair if there.

Use deodorant or perfume to stay fresh throughout. Opt for unscented options, as strong fragrances can clash. Apply fragrance on pulse points (wrists, neck, shoulder, forearm, elbow, chest) where it can diffuse naturally, but avoid rubbing it in; this dulls the scent's top notes.

Pro Tip: Remember less is more, choose a subtle fragrance that suits your personality.

Nail grooming is often overlooked but it is as essential as other things. Always trim and clean under your nails; this simple step shows how much attention you pay to details. Dirt and debris can easily accumulate under nails, so maintaining clean nails becomes necessary.

Pro Tip: Don’t hesitate to get a manicure if you want to go the extra mile.

When it comes to first dates, your smile is the best accessory you can wear, and good oral hygiene is essential for making a lasting impression. For a bright, healthy smile, brush twice a day, floss daily, and use mouthwash for that extra freshness.

Avoid last-minute fixes like mints or gum; instead, incorporate good oral hygiene into your daily routine. Here consistency is the key - make brushing and flossing part of your everyday ritual so you can focus on enjoying the moment rather than worrying about your breath.

Pro Tip: Keep sugar-free gum handy for a quick breath refresher.

chunks.heading: You’re Ready For Your First Date!
chunks.content:
- Keep it natural and comfortable: Think effortless charm rather than over-the-top glam as over-styling can be a major turn-off.

- Subtle scents over heavy fragrances: Follow the "arm's length" rule - apply your fragrance so that it lingers just out of reach, creating an inviting aura without overpowering the senses.

- Avoid last-minute experimentation: Stick to your go-to products and routines like shampoo, moisturizer, or styling cream which are tried and tested - trustworthy friends who never lets you down.

- Prioritize basic hygiene: Neglecting it can be an immediate deal-breaker, so bring your simplicity to the table and focus on what truly matters.

First-date grooming is your golden ticket to making a dazzling impression! Think of it as stealing the spotlight by showcasing the best version of yourself. By focusing on personal hygiene, choosing an outfit that expresses your style, and perfecting your grooming routine, you can create an irresistible vibe.

The real secret? While looking well-groomed is essential, your authenticity is the show-stopper because when you are you, you radiate, also drawing others in. So, go on your first date with flair and charisma; after all, the most impressive thing is to express the real you out loud!

blogs.title: How to Identify Your Face Shape

chunks.heading: STEP 2: MEASURE YOUR FACE
chunks.content:
Human face is like a canvas and like every artist we strive to create our own identity by adding new elements on it. Women are more expressive on this front and do so with the help of makeup, hairstyles, tattoos, piercings and managing facial hair. On the other hand, men are more conservative in letting their guards down, and stick to experimenting only with hairstyles and facial hair (a moustache or a beard). Notwithstanding, both hairstyles and beard styles can really add to one’s personality if they are customized to suit one’s face. This makes it extremely important for you to identify your face shape and go for styles that make you look good.

The first step into finding your face shape is to understand the cross-section of your face. Your face can be divided into three parts horizontally and one part vertically. These are your forehead, the breadth of your face or your cheekbones and your jawline. The vertical part is simply the length of your face from top to bottom.

Once you understand the four parts of your face, it’s easy to measure them, either with a measuring tape or simply with your fingers. Doing it with a measuring tape will ensure more precision, so we suggest you take down notes for reference. If you are confident about your estimation skills, measuring your face with your hands is the easiest way to circumvent any complications and confusions.

Measuring the forehead

Place the edge of your measuring tape on the left side of your hairline and draw it towards the right side of your hairline.

Measuring the breadth of your face

Identify the highest part of your cheekbones by feeling both sides of your face. If you’re unable to make out the exact spot, gently run your fingers down the edges of your eyes and you’ll feel a high point beyond which the contours will begin to slide downwards. Take the measurement from the highest point on the right to the highest point on the left.

Measuring the jawline

Measure from the centre of your chin to the area where your jaw angles upwards, below the left ear. This is one half of your jawline, so either repeat the same process on the right side as well, or simply double the measurement from one side.

When doing it with your hands just measure the cross section of your jawline with your middle finger and thumb horizontally. You’ll be amazed how accurately this can help you identify your face shape.

Measuring the length of your face

Measure top to bottom from the centre of your hairline to the last point of your chin.

chunks.heading: When Length > Breadth
chunks.content:
Face shapes can be broadly divided into 8 categories under 2 basic structures, based on multiple combinations of the above measurements. This is not an exhaustive list and we don’t claim that these are the only face cuts in the human race. It’s purely based on the most common face shapes around the world.

There are two face types where the face is as long as it is wide. So, they resemble the two most symmetrical geometrical designs of round and square. However, the two differ in the jawline and the angles they form at their edges.

Round Face

A round face has similar measurement of the length and cheekbones. The forehead and jawline, while usually smaller than the cheekbones, also have similar measurements. A round face will always have rounder edges on the jawline.

Square Face

A square face, like a round face, also has similar measurements of length and breadth of the face. The jawline will be the widest part of the face and will have more angular edges.

The most common proportion of a human face is when the length of the face is bigger than the width. This leads to multiple permutations and combinations and hence different face shapes in this category.

Rectangular Face

If the forehead, cheekbones and jawline are fairly equal to each other, and the jawline has a straight angular cut, sometimes leading to an almost flat chin, it is safe to call the face shape rectangle.

Oblong Face

When the face, just like a rectangular face, the forehead, cheekbones and jawline measure the same, but the angle at which the jawline moves up is more rounded than sharp, then then the face shape is oblong.

Diamond Face

A diamond face has a narrow forehead that measures almost the same as the jawline, but has wide cheekbones. The chin is quite prominent among this category of face shape and meets the jawline at a sharp angle.

Oval Face

Just like a diamond face cut, an oval face has narrow forehead and jawline measuring almost the same, with wide cheekbones. The only different is that the jawline is rounded at the edges, leading to a heavy look at the base.

Heart Face

A heart face has descending measurements of forehead, cheekbones and jawline, meaning the forehead would be the widest part of the face, followed by the cheekbones and a narrow jawline. The chin is usually sharp and small.

Triangular Face

Consider this to be an inverted heart. The widest part of a triangle face is the jawline, followed by cheekbones and a narrow forehead. The jawline is usually flat.

chunks.heading: IN SHORT...
chunks.content: Once you know your face shape, you can play around with your beard and hairstyles by donning the one that creates a balance in your face. For instance, if you have a heart face and you decide to go for the popular ducktail beard style with longer hair around your chin, you will end up making your face look too long for aesthetics. Happy styling!

blogs.title: Losing Hair? Reasons and Quick Daily Fixes

chunks.heading: What makes men LOSE HAIR?
chunks.content:
As men, one of the biggest fears we have is losing our hair. It makes us want to constantly check on our hair, running our fingers through them, hoping to find nothing in our palms.

This fear becomes a reality when we see too many strands of hair on our hands. But you shouldn’t be alarmed at the first instance you notice this, as it is normal to lose about 50-100 strands of hair each day. The problem starts when your hair growth cycle is disrupted and your hair begins to fall out too often too quickly.

The reason? It could be anything from pollution, stress, anxiety, work pressure, bad diet, to harmful chemicals that we slap on ourselves daily. All this affects our hair growth cycle, which needs proper medical attention.

Genetics is the biggest culprit when it comes to hair loss. If your family tree has a history of baldness, then there is a high chance that you might lose your hair. However, to assume you will lose your hair just because your family has a history of male-pattern baldness is not right. The reason for your hair loss could be very different and you need to dive deep into it to understand the true reason.

Hormonal Changes in the body is the other reason for sudden hair fall. A hormone called Dihydrotestosterone DHT is majorly responsible for shrinking down the hair follicles. As a result, your hair becomes thinner and falls eventually.

Some underlying conditions like diet and stress significantly contribute to hair thinning and eventually, hair loss. It can be rooted in either inadequate levels of testosterone levels or excess estrogen in the male body.

Poor lifestyle choices like irregular sleeping patterns affect your hair too. Melatonin is a hormone that regulates the sleep cycle and keeps the hair growth at a healthy level. If you’re someone who stays up late for any reason you should know that sleep has a direct impact on your body's natural hormones. That is, a poor sleep routine reduces the amount of melatonin, potentially causing hair loss.

chunks.heading: Scalp Massages
chunks.content:
As the thinning starts, the hair strands shrink in size gradually until they get so thin that they just break off easily. It falls off and that's it. No matter what you do, it’s never coming back. Once it's gone, it's gone.

A large number of your hair follicles can start to shed during the hair thinning phase. As a result, the number of hair on your head looks sparse.

The good news is that hair loss due to stress is temporary, and there is a high chance to reverse it. So if you are in a stressful condition, this might help you stress down a bit. When your mind and body get out of that ‘STRESS’ zone, your hair growth cycle will return to normal, and your hair may show new growth.

So once you’re aware about the root causes of your hair fall it won’t take much time for you to treat the condition and stop the shedding.

Once you’re aware of the reason, you can do a few things to not only stop the hair fall but make your hair thick, luscious and healthy again. One of the ways to treat your hair loss is to add Bhringraj Oil to your head massages. Known for its Ayurvedic properties, it can do wonders for your hair. In addition to that, a few tweaks in your lifestyle can prove to be helpful. Let’s see what can work for you.

Get consistent with scalp massages. It can help your hair get thick and healthy like it used to be before. Do not use nails, use your fingertips and massage your scalp gently for 5 minutes every day. Scalp massages promote blood flow to the scalp, which encourages longer, thicker hair strands. Add oils with ingredients like Bhringraj and Onion to boost the health of your hair.

chunks.content:

This takes more time than usual, but we are sure you don't wanna lose your hair just because you want to save a few minutes.

After every shower, don’t rub your towel on your hair too harshly. Patting them dry is the most suitable way to dry them and should be followed as a routine to keep your hair healthy, even if they are not thinning. The other thing is to carefully brush your hair to avoid any breakage. Stay away from blowing them dry with a hair dryer, as this dries up your scalp and makes the hair weaker on the roots.

Get serious about nutrition. Consult a doctor and take the right hair supplements as prescribed. These supplements are mostly biotin, zinc, iron, and vitamins B, C, D, and E to make your hair regain their health. Additionally, do not take supplements as the only way to complete your nutritional deficiency. Remember, there is a reason why these are called ‘supplements’. They only supplement the nutritional gap in your diet. So, always try to get the maximum nutrition from your diet.

If you notice hair all around your pillow and sheet every morning you know it is time to do something about it. Regular pillow covers are not hair-friendly. When you move at night while sleeping, there is a high chance of tugs and pulls, leading to breakage in your hair. Avoid this and switch to silk pillow covers. One, it is way softer than cotton. Two, it is better for your skin. Three, it feels more luxurious than any other pillowcase. Once you switch to them, you are never going back.

chunks.heading: Frequently Asked Questions
chunks.content:
Follow all these tips, and in no time you will notice the difference. Additionally, avoid touching your hair too often; this only worsens the health of your hair. Even after trying everything, if you constantly lose hair and do not see a way out, consult a dermatologist.

Q. Does wearing a hat increase the chances of losing hair?

A. There is no direct relation between wearing a hat and losing hair, but it is slightly connected. Top-to-down pressure is not problematic, but a pulling motion is. So if your hat is too tight or you adjust it too vigorously on your head, it may lead to breakage. Also, for guys with longer hair, tying your hair too tightly may have a similar effect and end up in increased breakage.

Q. Does dry air from the air-conditioner make your hair weak?

A. Air conditioners make the air around them dry, so when you sit under them for long hours, your scalp may also get dehydrated, making your hair look lifeless, rough and frizzy – an ideal situation for inducing hair fall. To avoid this, use a hair serum that not only adds nutrition to your hair but also creates a moisture barrier and prevent moisture loss.

blogs.title: Top 6 Mistakes to Avoid BEFORE an Interview

chunks.content:
Let’s be honest, interviews are stressful. Whether it’s for your next job or the college you really, really want to get into, there’s always a hint of panic before an interview, no matter how prepared you are.

Here’s something no one ever tells you - Interviews are not just about getting all the answers right, dropping the important buzzwords, or ensuring your handshake is firm but not too tight. They’re also about how you present yourself.

Chances are, the way your interview goes is decided before you even say ‘Hello’.

The interviewer is noticing everything:

How you walk in.
How you sit.
How you look.
How comfortable you seem in your own skin (Yes, people can tell).

This isn’t a guide that tells you how to crack a big interview or where to find the best interview questions, we know you’re already preparing for that. This is about avoiding certain mistakes before an interview that can make you stand out… and not in a good way.

Let’s begin!

1. Grooming on the day of the interview

Most people treat getting ready for an interview like a last-minute activity.

Shower.
Shave.
Run.

And that’s how you end up with flimsy looks, razor burns, frizzy hair, and a subtle energy of “I’m barely holding it together.”

Wouldn’t it be better to push everything to the night before? From deciding what to wear to a quick skincare routine, doing things a day in advance helps you stay calmer on the interview day, and gives your skin some breathing room too.

Trust us, grooming the day before is far better than trying to cram everything into 30 minutes.

Here are a few things you can do the night before:

- Shave in advance so any skin irritation has time to calm down

- Exfoliate with a face scrub and end with a peel-off mask to make your skin look fresh throughout the interview

- Take a proper shower (not a rushed one)

- Moisturise with a good body lotion (this one’s non-negotiable, honestly)

2. The Care You Put Into Your Hair

Interview hair doesn’t need to be dramatic or overly styled. But it also shouldn’t look like you just rolled out of bed.

The sweet spot? Controlled yet natural.

You’ll get there by not using too many products, just enough to give your hair some structure and direction.

And it goes without saying, experimenting with your hair on the day of the interview is a big no-no.

That cool haircut you really want to try can wait a day or two.

3. Not (AI)ming For Authentic Answers

People can tell when you’re being genuine and when you’re repeating something you copied from your friendly AI chatbot.

Asking AI to write your answers and memorising them like a speech often comes across as inauthentic. Interviewers want to know you and your personality, not how well you can recite something that doesn’t even sound like your own words.

We’re not stopping you from preparing talking points beforehand. But your stories are yours to tell, without layers, without filters, and without any jhijhak.

4. Rough Patch With A Sweat Patch

We get it. You really want the job. You really want the interviewer to like you. It’s stressful.

And all that nervous energy? It often turns into sweat patches and BO you weren’t prepared for.

Use a roll-on deo instead of a spray to control your sweat and odour instead of just covering it up with fragrance. Plus, it's pretty neutral to be safely paired with a perfume of your choice. So, you won't just NOT be sweating like bacon but also smell great.

5. Virtually Careless

This one’s obvious. Just because your interview is virtual doesn’t mean you can treat it like a regular video call with your friend.

Make sure you've checked your internet connection and the camera on your laptop (Don’t use your phone) beforehand. If you're still struggling to see each other once the interview starts, you would look extremely unprofessional and inefficient. That is something they should find out on their own.

6. Bro, Where’s The Pep Talk?

Nothing says confidence like saying it to yourself.

Take ten minutes before the interview to calm your nerves and remind yourself of what makes you awesome.

Listing the top five things that make you stand out & make you a strong candidate for the role can completely change the energy you walk in with.

It’s tried and tested. The shift is mind-blowing!

In Conclusion…

We know what you’re thinking. No one is going to hire you just because you moisturise well or your beard looks great.

But trust us, they may not say it, but they’re taking notes on everything. Before your resume is processed, you are.

And the biggest mistake men make? Thinking that grooming for an interview is about impressing others.

It’s not.

It’s about not being distracted by your own discomfort.

Interviews aren’t just question-and-answer rounds. They’re conversations. They’re storytelling.

And no good story deserves distractions like itchy skin, sweat patches, nervous fumbling, or that nagging feeling that something about you feels…off.

blogs.title: What should be there in a men's grooming kit?

chunks.heading: 1. Face Wash Enriched With Superfoods
chunks.content:
The best thing about the time we live in is the fact that grooming routines are no longer limited to women. Nobody scorns at us when we look for the right skincare regimen for our skin type, with in fact several options at our fingertips, ranging from basic essentials to luxury indulgences. Whether you're a minimalist or a full-on grooming lover, there's something out there for everyone. But with so many choices, how do you know what you really need?

That's where your personal grooming kit comes in. So, let’s start from the start and take a peek into an essential guy’s grooming kit. Pull up your socks because this may just change your game!

Grooming has moved beyond just the means of looking good. It also affects how you feel within and leaves a long-lasting impression on the world around you. So, without going fancy, here are the absolute essentials that your grooming kit must have.

You need a deep cleansing face wash to remove dirt, oil, and impurities that accumulate on the surface of your skin all day. Even if you don’t spend time outdoors, you’d be surprised to know how much pollution permeates inside the four walls of our homes and offices. Now, some face washes not only cleanse your face, but also control excess sebum production, unclog the pores on your skin, and even de-tan it with skin-brightening extracts.

Look for face cleansers that are formulated with natural ingredients for added nourishment in your skin. Activated charcoal is an excellent add-on for guys’ skin, as it penetrates 5X deeper than cleansers without it and cleans the skin from within. Additionally, look for sulfate-free products that are safer for your skin and health.

Regularly using a face wash can improve your skin tone and texture. So, investing in a high-quality paraben and sulphate free face wash is the first step to head start with your personal grooming ‘A’ game.

Pro Tip: Buying face wash according to your skin type is the best way to get the desired results.

CTA: Face Wash For Oily & Acne-prone Skin

chunks.heading: 3. Non-sticky Lightweight Sunscreen
chunks.content:
The second essential for guys is a moisturizer, both for your face and body. You may feel you don’t need one when the temperature outside is high and humidity veils your skin under beads of sweat, but it’s this fluctuation in the weather conditions indoors and outdoors that makes it extremely important for you to always keep a moisturizer by your side.

Look for an ultra-hydrating moisturizer that replenishes any lost moisture in the skin, and at the same time doesn’t clog the pores or ends up making the skin greasy. Read the label for non-comedogenic options. The best hydrating agents to look for in a good moisturizer are Shea Butter, Avocado extracts, Aloe Vera, Jojoba Oil, and Argan Oil. They can really lift up your daily skincare routine and enhance the overall feel and appearance of your skin.

Pro Tip: A lightweight and non-greasy moisturizer is ideal for oily skin, while creamy moisturizers work better for dry skin.

Sunscreen is a non-negotiable item in a grooming kit for guys, no matter what the season is. Even when the sun appears to be waning or hidden behind the clouds, its ultraviolet rays can still penetrate through the atmosphere and ultimately into your skin, causing dryness, sunburns, premature ageing and even serious skin conditions like eczema or cancer.

Look for a non-sticky sunscreen with at least SPF 30 to ensure basic protection. If you’re planning a trip to the hills or the beach where your exposure is planned to be longer than 20 minutes, up the SPF number accordingly. Remember, higher SPF sunscreen products may be thicker in viscosity and end up looking oily on the skin. A hack to avoid this is to look for gel-based sunscreen. For added convenience, consider a moisturizer that includes SPF, allowing you to combine steps in your routine.

Pro Tip: In order to avoid the extra oil associated with high SPF sunscreen creams, pick up a gel-based one instead.

chunks.heading: 5. Shaving Foam Prepared From Natural Ingredients
chunks.content:
Most guys keep a beard in some form or the other. And even if you only have a stubble, those strands on your chin still need some nourishment. Enter beard oil, that keeps the beard conditioned, organized and provides the much-needed nutrition to the hair follicles underneath. It also hydrates the skin, as the beard cover makes skincare difficult in those areas. Additionally, using a good beard oil also protects you from bacterial infections, itchiness, and beard dandruff.

While there are multiple options available in the market, it’s easy to identify which beard oil to go for. Look for one with natural ingredients like jojoba oil, argan oil, cedarwood oil, or almond oil. Avoid those with sulfates and parabens as they can really irritate your skin.

Pro Tip: Make sure that the scent of the beard oil is not overpowering, as it is close to your nose and you don’t want to be nauseous. Choose natural fragrances that are not too strong.

Shaving foam is one of the prime shaving essentials. It is a soft and fluffy protective barrier between the sharp razor blades and your sensitive skin but its effectiveness varies as per its composition. Mainly it contains, one, foam-generating components (surfactants) for lathering up your face, two, softeners (emollients) making your hair velvety so that razor can cut through easily, and, third, assisting agents responsible for its thickness, fragrance, and reducing the risk of cuts and nicks. If it has the presence of naturally extracted ingredients like Aloe vera, Argan Oil, Coffee, Nut Seed Oil, Menthol, and Olive Oil, then it is a pulse as it makes the shaving foam 2x creamier and safer.

Apart from guarding your skin against friction and irritation during shaving, it also leaves your skin on a cleansed, hydrated, and nourished note.

Fortunately, a comprehensive range of shaving foam is available to choose from, as per your liking and suitability. Like if you have oily and mild acne-prone skin, you can go for anti-inflammatory and antiseptic shaving foam powered by the goodness of turmeric, saffron, and tea tree oil. For dry skin, you can go for shaving foam with ingredients like oats that moisturize and soothe your skin after shaving. Activated charcoal-based shaving foam is perfect for normal skin, it would be best if it has Indian superfoods.

Pro Tip: Use shaving foams that are cruelty-free, SLS-free, and paraben-free to avoid unnecessary chemical reactions.

chunks.heading: 6. Dependable And Smart Razor With Lubricating Strip
chunks.content:
The razor is going to be the hero of your shaving affair and choosing the wrong one can turn into a nightmare. So, check the sharpness and quality of the razor beforehand rather than regretting it later. It would be much better if you pick a razor with curved blades. The razor with curved blades is designed to provide a better angle that cuts down hair effortlessly, allowing smooth and swift glides for a safer shave.

After the curved blades, the number of blades in a razor matters as well. More the blades your razor has, the closer the shave you are going to experience. The multi-blade system works on a mechanism where the first blade usually lifts the hair and other blades cut hair to the lowest level possible. To let you embrace, a smoother shave and long-lasting finish with the least risk of nicks and cuts.

It is a bounce if it has a pivoting head and lubricating strip to give an edge throughout your shaving process. As the pivot head helps easy maneuvering of the razor along the contours of your face, thus making it not only more comfortable but also safer. Simultaneously, the lubricating strip provides you a gentle cushioning while you glide the razor on your skin ensuring a close shave without causing nicks or cuts, even perfect for sensitive skin.

If you want to get the closest shave safely, then a razor with 6-blades should be your first choice, toughest on the facial hair but smoothest on your skin.

Pro Tip: To soothe your skin and reduce redness or irritation post shave you can use aftershave products.

chunks.heading: 8. Deep Cleansing Body Wash
chunks.content:
Generally, guys don’t give much attention to the beard like they tend to give to their hair. But for a fact, your beard needs that care and conditioning too. Using the shampoo and conditioner especially put together for beard care can bring a noteworthy difference. As they not only keep your beard clean and free from bacteria build-up but also maintain its moisture and manageability.

When choosing shampoo, keep in mind your specific hair concerns. Look for anti-dandruff shampoos if you struggle with flakes, or opt for products that promote hair growth if you’re experiencing thinning. Follow up with a conditioner to keep your hair soft and manageable. For men, who may face hair issues due to climate change and lifestyle transformation, going right with your beard care products is highly recommended.

Pro Tip: Using sulfate-free products preserves your hair’s natural oils.

Adding standard body wash can transform your daily shower experience. Unlike traditional soap, body washes are formulated to cleanse without your skin losing out on its natural oils. The moisturizing ingredients in it leave your skin feeling refreshed and hydrated. Men often dealing with Hyperhidrosis, a naturally formulated body wash can help you feel clean, odorless, non-greasy and active throughout the day.

Like other grooming products, select a body wash suitable to your skin type. If you have dry skin, look at ingredients like shea butter or coconut oil. For oily skin, a body wash gel can help control excess oil. According to a survey by the International Journal of Dermatology, men are increasingly opting for body washes over bar soaps.
