chunks.content:
Whether it's a crucial business meeting, a first date, or a night out with friends, you are setting the vibe for the same. And, having a personally curated grooming kit by your side, you don’t need to worry about your well-groomed look.

So, take the time to curate your grooming kit, to experiment with new products and techniques, and discover what brings out the best in you. As you're not just grooming your body; you're grooming your mind, your spirit, and your personality at the same time.

blogs.title: Antiperspirant vs Deodorant

chunks.heading: What Are Antiperspirants, And How Do They Work?
chunks.content:
(Learn the basic key differences between the two)

Antiperspirant functions in a way that blocks your sweat glands and reduces the amount you perspiration when you sweat. Go for them if you sweat excessively and especially want to reduce sweating in the underarms.

Deodorant is designed to mask the odour that develops as a result of sweating. Go for them if you don’t sweat as much and are only looking for a quick solution to smelling better and limiting the odour.

Antiperspirants are specialised formulations that are designed to control the amount of sweat that you experience after doing some physical activity or due to exposure to hot and humid environments.

They are formulated with aluminium chloride and other aluminium compounds. But before anything more on this, do you know what’s the logic and mechanism of sweating?

When you do a physical activity or are present in a hot and humid environment, your body heats up.

Too much of this heat would cause your internal organs to malfunction, so as a defence mechanism your body pushes out water in the form of sweat in order to and to cool it down through evaporation. This process is called perspiration.

But interestingly, the sweat doesn’t have any smell of its own. It turns into a nasty smell only when the bacteria sitting on our skin comes in contact with it, and stays in contact for a long time.

That’s why your arms don’t smell bad, but your armpits do. Because the sweat quickly evaporates from your arms but stays pressed between the skin in your armpits and gets that extra time needed for the bacteria.

Hence, you need an anti-perspirant to control the sweating in those areas.

Application tip: Apply antiperspirant before going to bed to block excessive sweating while you sleep.

chunks.heading: Which One Should You Choose?
chunks.content:
Deodorants, on the other hand, do not stop the sweating. They are designed to control or in simple terms mask the odour when you sweat.

We’ve already explained above how sweat doesn’t have an odour of its own, it’s just the bacteria acting up, causing the bad smell to knock on the door.

So, when you spray or rub a deodorant, it literally de-odour-ises your body, masking the foul smell behind and mask it with a pleasant one.

Most deodorants are alcohol-based, and they create a more acidic environment on your skin, which in turn decreases the odour. Many of them contain olfactive notes similar to a standard perfume and add fragrance.

But due to their diluted composition, they stays for a lesser duration than a perfume and need to be reapplied after regular intervals.

Application Tip: Apply the deodorant in the morning after shower on clean, dry skin. A good deodorant should last an entire day.

Both deodorants and antiperspirants have very singularly distinctive functions. So, go for antiperspirants if you have a problem of excessive sweating.

But if you’re only looking for odour management and just want to feel & smell fresh all day long, get a deodorant.

While both of them are considered to be fairly safe, antiperspirants can come with certain health risks for people with kidney issues.

Since antiperspirants block the sweat glands, people with a kidney function of less than 30% may have difficulty clearing the aluminium in antiperspirants out of their bodies efficiently.

chunks.heading: Are There Any Risks Involved
chunks.content:
It's not the product, it's the ingredients.

The best way out is to read the labels and understand if you might be allergic to anything mentioned there.

Sharing with you some of the possible risks below:

Skin Irritation: If you have sensitive skin, there is a high chance that your skin might not like either of them. The possible visible effects are redness, itching, or a rash when using deodorants or antiperspirants. Do a patch test before us and if you experience anything like this, stop right there and don’t continue with them. For people with normal skin they’re fairly safe.

Allergic Reactions: Many deodorants for men and antiperspirants have added fragrances in them along with preservatives, and other chemicals, all of which pose a risk of allergic reactions. You can easily find fragrance-free options if you already have a skin condition.

Aluminium Content from Antiperspirants: There has been some concern about the potential long-term health effects of aluminium content, which includes breast cancer and Alzheimer's disease. However, the data to support this is very limited and there is no evidence to back the relationship between aluminium in antiperspirants and these health conditions.

Staining: Antiperspirants pose a higher chance of stains on your clothes due to the presence of aluminium content. Apply them judiciously, so that you don’t have to worry about getting the stains off.

Compensatory Sweating from Antiperspirants: Since antiperspirants function by temporarily clogging the sweat glands, the aftermath of this may be increased sweating in other parts of the body.

Disruption of the Skin Microbiome: Both deodorants and antiperspirants can disrupt the natural order of bacteria on your skin. This disruption may have big implications for the health of your skin and your overall skin odour control situation.

chunks.heading: Frequently Asked Questions
chunks.content:
When walking through the deodorant vs. antiperspirant debate, it's essential to tailor your choice to your specific needs and body type. While both products are considered safe, it's important to be mindful of potential risks such as skin irritation and allergies. Additionally, when you transition from antiperspirants to Deodorants for Men, you might experience temporary increase in sweating, which will get to the normal state in a few days. So the tip here is to be well-informed about these products and consider how your skin might react to them, so you can make the right choice for your hygiene.

Q. A re there any natural or aluminium-free alternatives to antiperspirants?

A. Technically, there is nothing called a natural antiperspirant. But some say arrowroot powder and baking soda have a similar effect as an antiperspirant. However, we have not tried this and can’t recommend it to people looking for alternatives. Having said that, there are antiperspirants that come without aluminium compounds that you can check out.

Q. What is Antiperspirant Withdrawal?

A. Antiperspirant withdrawal is an excessive sweating condition when you switch from antiperspirants to deodorants. This situation is temporary, and it usually lasts from a few days to a few weeks, depending on the body that adjusts to the new shift.
Q. Can I use deodorant and antiperspirant together?

A. Yes, you can find many products in the market that are a combination of deodorant and antiperspirants. They help you fight two problems with one product. They provide both odour control and sweat reduction. It's like getting the best of both worlds and that too with just one product.

blogs.title: Dry, Itchy Winter Skin? This One Habit Is Aging Indian Men Faster Than They Realise

chunks.heading: Why Your Skin Needs Winter Moisture
chunks.content:
Winter in India hits differently depending on where you live. Delhi mornings leave your skin feeling like sandpaper. Mumbai's "winter" barely registers. Bangalore gets pleasantly cool but somehow still dries you out. Yet most guys treat moisturizer like it's optional—something their mom nags about.

Here's what's actually happening: cold air holds less moisture. Indoor heating (or those oil heaters) strips humidity further. Your skin loses water faster than it can replace it. That tight, itchy feeling? That's your skin barrier cracking under pressure, literally.

Dry skin isn't just uncomfortable—it ages you faster, makes you look tired, and creates the perfect environment for irritation and infections. One quality body lotion solves all of this, yet most men still think lotion is "too much effort" or "feels weird."

At Bombay Shaving Company, we've formulated a body lotion that addresses the main reason guys avoid moisturizer: that sticky, greasy aftermath that makes you feel like you need another shower.

The Science of Dry Skin:

Your skin has a protective barrier—think of it as invisible cling wrap keeping moisture in and irritants out. Cold weather, hot showers, and harsh soaps damage this barrier. Water escapes faster than your body can produce natural oils to seal it in.

Result: flaky patches, ashiness (especially visible on elbows and knees), that cracked heel situation you've been ignoring, and overall discomfort that low-key ruins your day.

Beyond Just Feeling Better:

Moisturized skin heals faster from nicks and cuts. It's more resistant to infections. Fine lines and wrinkles appear less pronounced. Colors look better on hydrated skin—your clothes literally look better when your skin isn't dull and ashy.

Plus, severely dry skin itches. You end up scratching unconsciously, causing more damage, triggering more itching. It's a cycle that one good lotion breaks immediately.

The Barrier Function:

Healthy skin barrier = moisture stays in, bacteria stay out, you look like you have your life together. Damaged barrier = constant moisture loss, vulnerability to irritation, and that perpetual "rough around the edges" appearance.

chunks.heading: The 3-in-1 Body Lotion: Your Winter Essential
chunks.content:
The Greasy Factor:

Traditional lotions sit on skin forever, leaving that slick film that attracts lint, makes your phone slippery, and generally feels disgusting. You feel dirtier after applying than before.

Our 3-in-1 Fast-Absorbing Body Lotion solves this. Actually absorbs instead of sitting on the surface. Non-sticky, lightweight formula means you can get dressed immediately without that gross tacky feeling.

The Time Excuse:

"I don't have time for skincare routines." Fair. But we're talking 30 seconds post-shower. Literally less time than scrolling one Instagram reel. If you have time to dry off with a towel, you have time to apply lotion.

The Masculinity Trap:

Somehow moisturizer got coded as unmanly. Meanwhile, professional athletes, actors, and successful businessmen all maintain their skin because they understand presentation matters. Dry, cracked skin doesn't project confidence—it projects neglect.

Face, Hands, and Body Coverage:

One bottle handles everything. No need for separate hand cream, body lotion, and face moisturizer cluttering your bathroom. Simplicity for guys who want results without complexity.

Coconut for Intense Hydration:

Coconut oil penetrates deeply instead of sitting on the surface. It's been used in Indian skincare for centuries because it actually works—especially in our climate. Provides that moisture your skin desperately needs without feeling heavy.

Cocoa for Nourishing Glow:

Cocoa butter isn't just about moisture—it brings vitamins and antioxidants that improve skin tone and texture. That healthy glow people associate with "taking care of yourself" comes partly from properly nourished skin.

3X Goodness Strategy:

Locks moisture in using barrier-strengthening ingredients. Strengthens your skin's natural protective layer so it holds moisture better long-term. Restores natural tone by addressing dryness-induced dullness. It's not just treating symptoms—it's fixing the underlying problem.

Universal Skin Type Compatibility:

Dry skin gets intense hydration. Oily skin gets moisture without extra grease (yes, oily skin still needs moisturizer—dehydrated oily skin produces even more oil). Normal skin stays balanced. Sensitive skin gets relief without irritation.

Safe Indian Formula:

Dermatologically tested and approved. Paraben-free and sulphate-free. Made in India specifically for Indian skin dealing with Indian weather conditions. No adapting international products meant for different climates.

chunks.heading: Addressing Specific Winter Skin Issues
chunks.content:
Post-Shower Application (The Critical Window):

Your skin is most receptive to moisture within three minutes of showering. Don't completely dry off—pat until slightly damp, then apply lotion. Traps that surface moisture while adding more.

Morning Routine:

Quick shower (lukewarm, not scalding hot—hot water strips oils). Pat partially dry. Apply lotion focusing on typically dry areas: elbows, knees, shins, hands. Get dressed. You're done in under a minute.

Evening Application:

Even if you don't shower, apply to hands and face before bed. Nighttime is when skin does most of its repair work. Giving it moisture to work with improves results.

Problem Area Focus:

Elbows and knees get driest fastest—extra application here. Heels crack in winter—don't ignore your feet. Hands constantly exposed to washing—reapply after handwashing in dry weather.

Pre-Shave Prep:

Moisturized skin shaves better. Apply lotion 10-15 minutes before shaving if you have time. Softer skin means fewer nicks and less irritation.

Post-Gym Essential:

Shower after workout, apply lotion immediately. Gym environments (especially heated) dry skin aggressively. Post-workout is prime moisturizing time.

Travel Necessity:

Flights and air-conditioned hotels devastate skin moisture. Travel-size lotion in carry-on saves you from arriving at your destination looking dehydrated and rough.

Before Important Events:

Wedding? Big meeting? Date? Apply lotion the night before and morning of. You'll look noticeably more put-together. Well-moisturized skin photographs better—seriously.

Ashy Elbows and Knees:

Daily application with focus on these areas transforms them within a week. The ashiness comes from extreme dryness—moisture fixes it completely.

Cracked Heels:

Apply thick layer to heels before bed, wear socks overnight. Repeat nightly for a week. Transforms even severely cracked heels. Maintenance application thereafter keeps them smooth.

Dry, Flaky Hands:

Keep lotion at your desk. Apply after every handwashing in winter. Hand skin has fewer oil glands—it needs external moisture more than other areas.

Itchy, Irritated Skin:

Often caused by barrier damage. Consistent moisture repairs the barrier, stopping the itch cycle. Takes 3-5 days of regular application to see major improvement.

Face Dryness Without Greasiness:

The lightweight formula works perfectly for face moisture without causing breakouts. Apply after face wash, before bed especially.

chunks.heading: Why Winter Demands Different Skincare
chunks.content:
Applying to Bone-Dry Skin:

Lotion works by trapping moisture. Applying to completely dry skin means there's less moisture to trap. Post-shower application when skin is slightly damp maximizes effectiveness.

Using Too Little:

Quarter-sized amount for each arm, each leg. More for torso. Don't be stingy—you want even coverage, not sparse spotting.

Skipping "Non-Visible" Areas:

Back of your arms, back of thighs, back in general—these dry out too even if you can't see them easily. Full body means full body.

Only Applying When You Remember:

Consistency beats intensity. Daily light application works better than occasional heavy application. Make it automatic like brushing teeth.

Wrong Post-Application Timing:

Give it 60 seconds to absorb before getting dressed. Fast-absorbing doesn't mean instant. That minute prevents the dreaded lint-stick situation.

Ignoring Hands:

Your hands age you faster than your face because they're constantly exposed and frequently washed. They deserve dedicated attention.

Summer vs. Winter Skin:

Summer brings humidity, sweat, and natural oil production. Your skin stays relatively hydrated on its own. Winter reverses all that—dry air, less natural oil, constant moisture loss.

Indoor Heating Impact:

Room heaters, car heaters, office climate control—all suck moisture from air and skin. You might not notice the gradual drying until your skin's already compromised.

Hot Shower Temptation:

Cold mornings make hot showers irresistible. But prolonged hot water strips skin oils aggressively. Lukewarm water cleans just as well without the damage—then lotion seals in moisture hot showers would otherwise strip away.

Clothing Factor:

Wool sweaters, synthetic thermals, rough fabrics—winter clothing creates more friction against dry skin, causing irritation. Moisturized skin handles this friction better.

chunks.heading: Making It Actually Happen
chunks.content:
Starting Young:

Skin damage accumulates. Starting proper moisturizing in your 20s means better skin in your 40s. Prevention beats correction.

Consistency Over Products:

One good lotion used daily beats five expensive products used sporadically. Habit matters more than having every product ever made.

Listening to Your Skin:

Extra dry day? Apply more. Healing from sunburn? Extra application helps. Skin tells you what it needs if you pay attention.

Seasonal Adjustment:

Winter requires more frequent application. Summer might need lighter coverage. Adjust based on how your skin feels, not rigid schedules.

The Professional Advantage:

Studies show people perceive individuals with healthy skin as more competent, trustworthy, and successful. Fair or not, presentation affects perception. Good skin contributes to professional credibility.

The Comfort Factor:

Dry skin creates constant low-level discomfort. You don't notice until it's gone, then you realize you've been unnecessarily uncomfortable for months.

The Aging Reality:

Moisturized skin develops fewer fine lines and wrinkles. Starting now means looking younger longer. It's literally anti-aging in a bottle.

The Practical Benefit:

Clothes feel better against moisturized skin. You're not constantly pulling at itchy collars or scratching through pants. Day-to-day comfort improves noticeably.

If consistent moisturizing doesn't improve severe dryness after two weeks, see a dermatologist. Persistent extreme dryness sometimes indicates underlying conditions like eczema or psoriasis requiring medical treatment.

If you develop rashes, burning, or worsening irritation from lotion, stop using and consult a professional. While rare with dermatologically-tested products, individual sensitivities exist.

Placement Strategy:

Keep lotion where you'll see it. Next to your towel works. On your nightstand reminds you for evening application. Visible = used.

Phone Reminders:

Set daily reminders for first two weeks until it becomes automatic. Habit formation takes time—technology can bridge that gap.

Linking to Existing Habits:

Right after showering already happens daily. Attach lotion application to that existing routine. Habit stacking works.

Tracking Results:

Take a photo of your worst dry skin area. Apply lotion consistently for one week. Compare. Visual proof motivates continued use.

chunks.heading: Your Skin Investment
chunks.content:
How much lotion should I use?

Quarter-sized amount per limb. More for torso. Enough for even, thin coverage—not thick globs.

Can I use this on my face daily?

Yes, it's formulated for face, hands, and body. Lightweight formula won't clog pores or cause breakouts.

Will this make oily skin more oily?

No. Dehydrated oily skin produces more oil trying to compensate. Proper moisture can actually reduce oiliness.

How long until I see results?

Immediate: skin feels softer, less tight. 3-5 days: visible reduction in flakiness. One week: significant texture improvement. Two weeks: transformation complete.

Can I use this in summer?

Yes, though you might need less frequent application. Skin needs moisture year-round, just varying amounts.

Does this work on severely cracked skin?

Yes, especially with consistent application. Severe cases might need twice-daily application initially, then maintenance once healed.

Is this safe for sensitive skin?

Dermatologically tested and approved. Paraben and sulphate-free formula minimizes irritation risk. Patch test if you're especially sensitive.

Can women use this?

Absolutely. Skin is skin. Gender-neutral formula works for everyone.

How is this different from expensive international brands?

Comparable ingredients and effectiveness at fraction of the price. Made specifically for Indian climate conditions, not adapted from international formulas.

Should I apply before or after getting dressed?

After, once lotion has absorbed (about 60 seconds). Prevents transfer to clothes.

You spend money on clothes, shoes, cologne—all external presentation. Your actual skin is the foundation everything else sits on. Neglecting it while perfecting everything else is like building a house on cracked foundation.

One bottle costs less than two coffees. Lasts weeks. Transforms how you look and feel daily. The return on investment is absurd when you actually think about it.

Most guys who start proper moisturizing wonder why they suffered through years of dry, uncomfortable skin. It's not complicated. It's not time-consuming. It's just basic maintenance that somehow got skipped.

The lotion exists. The science is clear. The benefits are proven. The only question is whether winter will find you with healthy, comfortable skin or dealing with the same dry, cracked situation you've ignored for years.

blogs.title: How to choose the right sunscreen

chunks.heading: Broad Spectrum
chunks.content:
Here’s a fun task for you.

Ask all the men sitting next to you right now whether they use sunscreen. Chances are, they don’t.
And the number of people who give you that answer will be more shocking than you’d think.

Why? Because most men don’t know what to get or think they don’t need it at all.

Let’s fix that.
We’ll break down what you should actually look for in a sunscreen, and how to use it properly.

Don’t worry!

- ❌You don’t need the most expensive sunscreen

- ❌You don’t need 5 different types

- ❌You don’t need a 10-step routine

SPF is the first thing everyone looks at. But it’s also the one thing most people don’t fully understand.

SPF = Sun Protection Factor

It tells you how well a sunscreen protects your skin from UVB rays (the ones that cause sunburn).

And here’s what the numbers actually mean:

- SPF 30 blocks about 97% of UVB rays

- SPF 50 blocks about 98%

However, the numbers don’t mean much if you’re not:

- Applying enough

- Reapplying

- Using it daily

Because even the highest SPF won’t help if you’re barely using it or skipping it altogether.

When a sunscreen says ‘broad spectrum’, it means it protects your skin from both types of UV rays.

- UVB rays cause sunburn

- UVA rays cause tanning, pigmentation, premature ageing, and long-term skin damage

And here’s the part most people don’t know:

UVA rays are present all day, all year. Even when it’s cloudy and even when you’re indoors near windows.

So if your sunscreen doesn’t say broad spectrum, you’re only doing half the job.

chunks.heading: White Cast
chunks.content:
Let’s be honest. Most men don’t skip sunscreen because they don’t care, they skip it because it feels terrible.

- Too sticky. Too shiny. Too oily.

- And sometimes, it leaves that dreaded white cast.

At that point, it’s straight to the back of the shelf till it expires and then is thrown away.

That’s why choosing the right texture matters more than anything else.

If you have oily skin

You need something that:

- Absorbs quickly

- Doesn’t leave a shine

- Feels lightweight

Look for:

- Gel-based formulas

- Water-based formulas

- Matte finish

And just FYI, not all sunscreens make your skin oily. The ones wrong for your skin do.

If you have dry skin

You can get more out of your sunscreen than just sun protection.

Go for:

- Cream-based formulas

- Sunscreens with hydrating ingredients like Hyaluronic Acid or Niacinamide

This way, you’re moisturising and shielding your skin in just one step. Efficient and effective.

If you have sensitive or acne-prone skin

You don’t need to avoid sunscreen, you just need to choose better.

Look for:

- Non-comedogenic formulas (won’t clog pores)

- Lightweight textures

- Minimal or no added fragrance

Breakouts aren’t caused by sunscreen itself. They are caused by using the wrong formulation for your skin.

This one’s important, especially for Indian skin tones.

A sunscreen that leaves a white or grey cast looks unnatural, feels uncomfortable, and gets skipped.

And anything you skip is useless.

So look for sunscreens that clearly say ‘no white cast’ on the packaging or are designed to blend seamlessly into your skin.

chunks.heading: In conclusion…
chunks.content:
Your environment matters more than you think.

If you live in a hot, humid place or have an active lifestyle, your sunscreen needs to keep up.

Look for sweat-resistant or water-resistant formulas that stay on for longer periods of time.

Because if it melts off in 20 minutes, it’s not doing much for you.

If you think applying a tiny amount of sunscreen is enough, keep reading.

THE CORRECT AMOUNT

About two fingers’ worth of sunscreen for your face and neck.

Same applies to any other exposed skin that’s not covered by your clothes.

Anything less, and you’re not getting the protection mentioned on the label.

You can pick the right sunscreen, apply it perfectly, and still not get full protection if you forget about this one simple truth:

Sunscreens don’t last all day long.

You need to reapply every 2–3 hours if you’re:

- Outdoors

- Sweating heavily

- Wiping your face frequently

This is the difference between sunscreen that feels effective and sunscreen that actually is.

You need sunscreen. Full stop.

And no, it’s not complicated.

You don’t need a shelf full of products or a complicated routine. You just need:

- The right sunscreen for your skin type

- The right amount

- Consistent use

Because skipping this one step every day is much more dangerous than you think.

While tanning and pigmentation are visible concerns, long-term UV exposure can also lead to serious skin damage, including skin cancer.

Regular sunscreen use helps:

- Reduce cumulative UV damage

- Lower the risk of skin cancer over time

- Protect your skin’s overall health, not just appearance

This isn’t just about looking good. It’s about long-term protection.

blogs.title: How to Remove Tan from Your Face at Home

chunks.heading: HOW TO AVOID GETTING TANNED?
chunks.content:
Tanning is your skin’s response to exposure to the ultraviolet (UV) radiations from the sun. As soon as it comes in contact with the warm rays, your body starts producing melanin and Vitamin D. Melanin is a natural substance that gives colour to your skin and hair, and does double shifts to protect your eyes and skin from the same (photoprotection). So, more and more melanin gets produced in the body causing a visible darkening of the skin around the area directly in contact with sun rays.

Moderate exposure to sun causes moderate tanning which is not harmful to the body in any way. But getting overexposed causes sun burns, pigmentation, a depression in the immune system and premature ageing of the skin. Besides sun spots, your skin may also experience fine lines and wrinkles.

Tanning is a temporary event that leaves a long-lasting shadow on the surface it happens. The longer the exposure to sun, the longer it takes to recover from the skin darkening it causes. Most of us are too casual about it because the time we spend in the sun is limited, but you’d be surprised to know how you’re getting tanned bit by bit everyday without even noticing. If you wear a ring, just compare your skin tone from under the skin and that around it. The fairer portion is the original colour of your skin, which is somehow the only part of your hand that has managed to maintain it. The good news is, unlike stepping out in the sun, tanning is not inevitable. You can protect yourself from it by the following simple ways.

chunks.heading: HOW TO REMOVE TAN?
chunks.content:
Prevention is better than cure. You can’t aim for an unrealistic scenario where you don’t step out in the sun at all unless you find another source of energy that’s cleaner than the sun itself. Until then, keep your guards up against the bad guys transporting themselves along with the good sun rays. Who, you ask? Well, not the entire package emitted by the sun is harmful for the skin. But the UVA and UVB rays within the ultra violet range are extremely harmful for us. Not just for the skin, but also for the eyes and the entire immune system. So, make sure you apply a broad-spectrum sunscreen lotion with a high SPF to create a shield around all parts of your exposed skin and prevent tanning.

Early mornings are the best time to allow yourself some basking in the sun. Once you start feeling the heat, abort the mission immediately. Avoid stepping out in the sun for longer durations and if it is absolutely necessary do so at later hours of the day, wear sunscreen, eye shades, a hat and other protective clothing to safeguard yourself. Wearing all of them at once may not be possible every time you let yourself out, but you get the point: maximum defense.

There are many ways you can undo tanning on your skin, including elaborate home remedies and easy skincare rituals. The home remedies should be followed with caution as unsupervised application of highly acidic substances on skin may cause irritation. Let’s see how you can remove tan easily from your skin at home.

Lemon & Honey

Lemon juice is a strong bleaching agent, which helps lighten colour, including that of excess melanin in the form of tanning. Just mix it with some honey to make sure you don’t dry up your skin too much with the highly acidic texture of lemon. Apply this on your skin and let it stay for 30 minutes. Wash with cold water.

Turmeric & Besan

Turmeric is a popular ingredient in our culture that is used on skin to make it brighter and more radiant skin. This is due to the skin lightening qualities of the rhizome. Just add a spoonful of turmeric to a large bowl of besan and make a thin paste by adding water or milk. Apply it on your face and scrub it off right before it starts drying. This naturally exfoliates your skin and also helps remove tan over time.

Potato Juice

This may sound weird, but those with some background in science (or access to a wise grandmother) know that potato is also a natural bleaching agent. Just juice a raw potato and apply it on your face. Let it stay for 10 minutes till it’s completely dry. Rinse with cold water.

Activated Charcoal

chunks.heading: MYTHS AROUND TANNING
chunks.content:
Charcoal is one of the most trusted ingredients that can help you with managing skin tans. It helps remove dead skin cells and deliver even complexion due to its cleansing properties. The Charcoal De-tan & Detox kit from Bombay shaving Company is a complete skincare solution to reveal your natural glow by not only removing the tan but by detoxifying the skin as well. Follow the facewash, scrub, mask ritual regularly for best results.

Coffee

Coffee powder is a natural skin exfoliator and the caffeine present in it can help increase the glow of your skin. You can use it with lemon juice or milk. Add few drops of fresh lemon juice in coffee powder and make a paste. Apply it on the affected area and let it stay for 10 minutes before rinsing with cold water. Alternatively, make a thick consistency paste off coffee powder with milk and apply on the affected area. Rinse with lukewarm water after 10 minutes.

You can also go for the Coffee De-tan Facial Kit from Bombay Shaving Company and get ready made Face Wash, scrub, mask and face pack to remove the tan from your skin and give yourself a glowing face.

Cloudy skies Mean I Won’t Get Tanned.

It only sounds logical, right? But if all those horror movies are to be believed, the evil always gets you when you let your guard down. Clouds do allow small amounts of UV rays even through their dense cover. So, when you think you’re enjoying a cloudy winter afternoon strolling in the park, your skin is still producing extra melanin to shield it against the leaked ultra violet rays.

I Can Skip Tanning By Applying Moisturizer After Exposure to Sun.

You need to treat your skin with more than just a moisturizer to soothe the sunburns. All that a moisturizer can do is replenish some hydration to your dehydrated skin. But the sundried skin will still go through process of peeling.

An Umbrella Can Save Me From Sun Tan.

While we’ve seen way too many people holding their umbrellas over their heads as they walk in the sun, all it does is save them from the heat. The UV rays still make their way through the fabric of the umbrella and still burn your skin. Thick hats can help and, of course, the good old sunscreen.

I Can’t Get Tanned In Water.

This is how your senses play with you. When you’re in a pool on a hot day your body feels refreshingly cold because of the low temperature of the water, but the sun rays easily pierce through its surface and start working on your skin like it would on land. In fact, you end up getting even more burned because of all that reflection. Extreme tanning due to reflections happens in high altitude areas with snow.

chunks.heading: IN SHORT…
chunks.content: Use a sunscreen. There’s no escaping that unless you want to spend weeks and weeks recovering from the suntan. Use skincare regimens formulated with super ingredients like activated charcoal and coffee. They not only help you de-tan but also push extra benefits into your skin.

blogs.title: 10 Tips To Take Care of Your Skin In Winters

chunks.heading: 2. Use a humidifier.
chunks.content:
Winter is here, bringing with it dry, flaky skin and a never ending desire to hibernate under a warm blanket. But fear not! Your skin doesn’t have to suffer through the colder months. With a little bit of extra care and attention, you can keep your skin healthy and glowing all winter long. So, put on your warmest socks, grab a mug of hot cocoa, and let’s get started on how to take care of your skin in winters.

Follow these 10 skincare tips to keep your skin healthy and glowing all winter long.

Winter is the time of year when the air is crisp and cold, and your skin starts to feel drier than the desert. This is because the dry air around tries to compensate for its loss of moisture with your skin and steals away its hydration, leaving you (high and) dry. So, before you crawl back into bed and hide under the covers until spring, remember to moisturise! Look for a moisturizer that is oil-based, as it will help to seal in moisture better than a water-based one.

The dry air inside your home can be just as damaging to your skin as the cold winter air outside. A humidifier adds moisture back into the air, helping to keep your skin hydrated. But the benefits don’t stop just there. A humidifier can also help to alleviate cold and flu symptoms, reduce static electricity (remember your hair being pulled towards your sweater with an invisible energy, leaving it frizzy and difficult to style?), and make the air in your home feel warmer. So, go ahead and give your skin and hair some much needed TLC this winter by investing in a humidifier.

chunks.heading: 5. Protect your skin from the elements.
chunks.content:
While it may be tempting to take long, hot showers to warm up during the winter, they can actually cause your skin to dry up very quickly, leaving you feeling tight and uncomfortable. Try to limit your showers to 10-15 minutes, and use lukewarm water instead of hot water. This will preserve your skin’s natural oils and keep it hydrated. Not to mention, shorter showers are better for the environment and can even save you money on your water bills.

Dead skin cells can build up on the surface of your skin during the winter, leading to a dull, lifeless complexion. Regular exfoliation will help to remove these dead skin cells, revealing the healthy, glowing skin underneath. But that’s not all. This can also help to improve the appearance of fine lines and uneven skin tone, and it can help your skin products to work more effectively.

Use a scrub that features natural ingredients, like Charcoal, Coffee and other superfoods that nourish the skin along with the process of exfoliation.

Winters are the best time to bask in the sun and soak in the elusive Vitamin D. In many Indian cultures it is customary to spend a lot of time in the sun in winters as this is the only season that is gentle enough to expose yourself to the otherwise harsh rays. But just a few minutes in the sun can tan your skin and with each passing minute after that its harmful ultraviolet spectrum can have more negative reactions.

Here are some tips to protect your skin from the sun in winter:

- Use Sunscreen with high SPF (SPF30 and above) and make sure to apply it to all exposed skin, even on cloudy days.

- Wear protective clothing, such as long sleeves and pants, and a wide-brimmed hat to shield your face and neck from the sun.

- Seek shade when the sun’s rays are the strongest, which is typically between 10 AM and 4 PM.

- Avoid being outside for extended periods of time, especially at high altitudes when the sun’s rays are more intense.

- Wear sunglasses to protect your eyes and the delicate skin around them from harmful UV rays.

chunks.heading: 7. Use a face mask.
chunks.content:
Our consumption of water goes for a toss as soon as the temperatures fall. You may blame it on not feeling thirsty enough, but despite not sweating profusely you’re still losing enough moisture through other means. Make a habit of drinking at least 2 litres of water daily. Trust us, this is the bare minimum you could do to keep your skin hydrated.

A face mask can help to add hydration and seal in moisture, leaving your skin feeling soft and smooth, especially in the colder months when moisture loss is inevitable. Besides the obvious, a face mask can also help with the following during winters:

- To soothe, dry & chapped skin. If your skin is feeling dry and chapped due to the cold weather, a face mask can help soothe and calm the irritation. Look for masks that contain ingredients like aloe vera, honey or shea butter, which are known for their hydrating properties.

- To help with skin conditions. Some people may have skin conditions like eczema or dermatitis that flare up in the winters due to the dry air. A face mask can alleviate symptoms by providing additional hydration and nourishment to the skin.

Look for one that is formulated for your skin type, and use it once or twice a week for best results. Charcoal Face Wash from Bombay Shaving Company has a three-way approach towards your skin. It detoxes your skin, restores it and ultimately rejuvenates, with the help of additional ingredients besides activated charcoal (detoxes), like coffee extracts (reduces acne and breakouts) and Korean Ginseng extracts (brings new life to your skin with its anti-ageing properties).

chunks.heading: 10. Get Enough Sleep.
chunks.content:
The skin on your lips is thin and sensitive, making it prone to drying out during winters. Use a lip balm or chapstick that contains sunscreen to keep your lips hydrated and protect it from the sun’s harmful rays. Also, avoid licking your lips, as saliva can further dry out your lips and make them more prone to cracking. Gentle exfoliation with a light lip scrub or toothpaste can help you remove dead skin cells from your lips, but make sure you don’t hurt your skin and always follow this with a good lip balm.

Eating a healthy, well-balanced diet can have a big impact on the health and appearance of your skin. Make sure to include plenty of fruits, vegetables, and fatty acids in your diet to nourish your skin from the inside out. Take a print out of the following list and put it up on your refrigerator for daily reference and course correction:

☐ Drink plenty of water. At least 8 glasses every day.

☐ East plenty of fruits and vegetables that are rich in vitamins and minerals

☐ Get enough protein with sources like lean meat, beans and nuts

☐ Limit the intake of sugar and fatty foods that can acne and skin inflammation

☐ Eat foods rich in omega-3 fatty acids, found in foods like flaxseeds & walnuts

☐ Consider taking Vitamin E and Zinc supplements after a discussion with your general physician

Proper sleep is essential for maintaining healthy, glowing skin. It helps repair and regenerate skin cells, reduces stress and inflammation, and helps improve blood circulation. Aim for 7-9 hours of sleep each night to give your skin the rest it needs.

blogs.title: If You’re Still Using Soap on Your Face, Read This

chunks.heading: Understanding Your Skin Type
chunks.content:
Your face takes the brunt of everything—pollution, sweat, stress, late nights, that third cup of chai. Yet most guys treat facial skincare like an afterthought, splashing water and calling it done.

Here's the reality: the dirt you see on your face is maybe 30% of what's actually there. The rest sits in pores, mixing with oil, dead skin cells, and Delhi's finest air quality. That's your breeding ground for dull skin, breakouts, and looking perpetually tired even after eight hours of sleep.

Proper face washing isn't complicated skincare routine territory. It's basic maintenance that prevents problems before they start. At Bombay Shaving Company, we've formulated cleansers that actually work for Indian skin dealing with Indian conditions—humidity, pollution, and climates that swing from AC freeze to outdoor furnace within minutes.

Bar soap strips your face's natural oils, triggering oil glands to overproduce. You end up in a cycle: wash, feel tight and dry, get oily by noon, wash again. Repeat until your skin just gives up.

Face washes are pH-balanced for facial skin specifically. They clean without destroying your skin barrier—that invisible shield protecting you from bacteria, irritation, and looking like you haven't slept since 2019.

Different face washes target different concerns. Charcoal for deep cleaning and oil control. Coffee for de-tanning and brightness. Understanding what your skin actually needs beats buying whatever's on sale.

Oily Skin:

Shiny by midday, prone to breakouts, large visible pores. You've tried "oil-free" everything and still look like you ran a marathon by 3 PM. Needs deep cleansing without over-stripping.

Dry Skin:

Tight feeling after washing, flaky patches, fine lines more visible. Your skin drinks moisturizer and asks for more. Needs gentle cleansing that doesn't dehydrate further.

Combination Skin:

Oily T-zone (forehead, nose, chin), dry or normal cheeks. Most Indian men fall here thanks to climate variations. Needs balanced cleansing that doesn't over-dry or over-oil different areas.

Sensitive Skin:

Reacts to new products, gets red easily, burns or stings from harsh ingredients. Needs fragrance-free, minimal-ingredient formulas.

chunks.heading: Coffee Face Wash: De-Tan and Revitalize
chunks.content:
Activated bamboo charcoal works like a magnet for dirt. Not surface-level dust—the microscopic pollution particles, excess sebum, and impurities lodged deep in pores.

10X Deep Cleansing Power:

Regular face washes clean the surface. Charcoal pulls from deeper layers where pollution settles and bacteria breed. Think of it as the difference between sweeping your floor versus actually mopping.

Perfect for City Life:

If you commute through traffic, work in air-conditioned offices, or live anywhere near construction, pollution sits on your skin constantly. This face wash specifically targets those toxins before they cause damage.

Oil Control Without Tightness:

Removes excess sebum without triggering the overproduction cycle. Your skin feels clean, not stripped. Pores visibly shrink because they're actually empty of gunk.

Safe Formula:

No SLS or parabens means even sensitive skin handles it well. You get effective cleansing without chemical harshness.

Best for: Oily skin, combination skin, anyone dealing with visible pollution effects, men prone to blackheads and enlarged pores.

Coorg coffee isn't just for drinking anymore. Those same antioxidants that wake you up internally work externally to brighten and rejuvenate tired-looking skin.

De-Tanning Powerhouse:

Sun damage shows up as uneven tone, dark patches, and that perpetual "just returned from Goa" look even when you haven't traveled in months. Coffee extracts target melanin buildup without bleaching or harsh chemicals.

Matcha Tea + Niacinamide Combo:

Matcha brings antioxidants that fight skin aging. Niacinamide (Vitamin B3) reduces dark spots, evens tone, and keeps skin firm. This combination addresses both immediate concerns (dullness, tan) and long-term issues (fine lines, sagging).

Maintains Natural Oils:

Unlike harsh de-tan treatments that leave skin dry and flaky, this formula brightens while respecting your skin barrier. You look refreshed, not chemically processed.

100% Organic Coffee Experience:

No SLS, no parabens, just effective natural ingredients doing what they're supposed to do. Safe enough for daily use.

Best for: Dull skin, uneven tone, visible tan lines, men who spend significant time outdoors, combination to dry skin types.

chunks.heading: Building Your Complete Skincare Routine
chunks.content:
Face wash handles daily maintenance. The charcoal peel-off mask is your weekly reset button.

Skin Detoxification:

Activated charcoal in mask form sits on your skin longer than wash-off products, pulling out deeply embedded blackheads, whiteheads, and stubborn oil deposits. It's oddly satisfying watching all that gunk come off attached to the mask.

Blackhead Elimination:

Those tiny dark spots on your nose and chin aren't permanent. The peel-off action physically removes them along with dead skin cells and trapped sebum. Results you can literally see on the peeled mask.

Pore Unclogging:

Clogged pores lead to acne. Unclogged pores prevent breakouts before they start. Simple cause and effect.

1-2 Times Weekly:

Not daily—peel-off masks are intensive treatments. Once or twice weekly gives benefits without over-exfoliating. More isn't better here.

Safe for All Skin Types:

SLS and paraben-free formula means even sensitive skin can use it (though always patch test first). Works on oily skin's excess sebum and normal skin's occasional congestion.

Best for: Blackhead-prone skin, oily T-zones, pre-event skin prep, anyone wanting visibly clearer pores.

Morning Routine (5 Minutes):

Splash face with lukewarm water. Apply face wash—coffee for brightness, charcoal if you're especially oily. Massage for 30-60 seconds, focusing on oily zones. Rinse thoroughly with cool water. Pat dry gently. Follow with moisturizer if needed.

Evening Routine (7 Minutes):

Wash hands first (crucial step everyone skips). Apply face wash generously. Really massage—you're removing a full day of pollution, sweat, and stress. Rinse thoroughly. Pat dry. Apply moisturizer or serum if using.

Weekly Deep Clean (15 Minutes):

Once or twice weekly, after your evening cleanse, apply the charcoal peel-off mask. Avoid eyebrows, hairline, and facial hair unless you enjoy pain. Let dry completely (15-20 minutes—use this time to scroll Instagram guilt-free). Peel off slowly from bottom up. Rinse any residue. Moisturize immediately after.

chunks.heading: Addressing Specific Skin Concerns
chunks.content:
Using Hot Water:

Hot water strips natural oils aggressively. Lukewarm cleanses effectively without damage. Finish with cool water to close pores.

Washing Too Often:

Morning and night suffices for most men. Over-washing triggers oil overproduction. If you workout midday, rinse with water only—save face wash for proper cleansing sessions.

Rough Towel Drying:

Pat, don't rub. Your face skin is delicate. Aggressive towel action causes irritation and premature wrinkles.

Skipping Moisturizer:

Even oily skin needs hydration. When skin feels dry, it produces more oil to compensate. Light, oil-free moisturizers prevent this cycle.

Using Dirty Towels:

Face towels should be washed every 3-4 uses. Bacteria from old towels transfers back to clean skin. Defeats the entire purpose.

Not Removing All Product:

Face wash residue clogs pores just like dirt does. Rinse until water runs completely clear, then rinse twice more.

Acne and Breakouts:

Charcoal face wash twice daily helps prevent new breakouts by keeping pores clear. The peel-off mask once weekly removes deeper congestion. Consistency matters more than product quantity.

Dark Spots and Hyperpigmentation:

Coffee face wash used daily gradually fades spots through niacinamide action. Patience required—skin cell turnover takes weeks, not days.

Enlarged Pores:

Pores don't actually shrink permanently, but keeping them clean makes them appear smaller. Charcoal products excel here—regular use maintains results.

Dull, Tired-Looking Skin:

Coffee face wash's antioxidants combat free radical damage causing dullness. Consistent morning use brings noticeable brightness within two weeks.

Excess Oil Production:

Charcoal face wash removes oil without triggering overproduction. The key is not over-washing—stick to twice daily maximum.

Uneven Skin Tone:

Coffee's de-tanning properties work gradually. Pair with sunscreen during day (even if you're indoors—window UV exists) for maximum effect.

chunks.heading: Building the Habit
chunks.content:
Formulated for Indian Climate:

International products often assume temperate weather. Our formulas account for humidity, heat, and drastic AC-to-outdoor temperature shifts.

Pollution-Fighting Ingredients:

Indian cities rank among world's most polluted. Our charcoal products specifically target pollution-related skin damage other brands ignore.

Price-Value Balance:

Quality ingredients at accessible prices. You're not paying for imported shipping or luxury brand markups. Just effective skincare that works.

No Harsh Chemicals:

SLS-free and paraben-free across the range means sensitive skin safety without sacrificing cleaning power.

Got a wedding, date, or important meeting coming up? Strategic skincare helps.

Three Days Before:

Use charcoal peel-off mask to deep clean. This gives skin time to calm from any minor redness before the event.

Daily Leading Up:

Consistent face washing with coffee formula for brightness. Morning and night, no skipping.

Day Of:

Morning cleanse with coffee face wash. Cool water final rinse to minimize pores. Moisturize lightly. You'll look noticeably fresher in photos.

Both face washes and the peel-off mask travel well. TSA-friendly sizes exist. Pack in ziplock bags to prevent airport pressure explosions.

Hotel water varies wildly in quality. Bring your own products rather than trusting mystery amenities that might irritate skin right before important meetings.

Most guys quit skincare because they expect overnight miracles. Real results take 2-3 weeks of consistency.

Start simple: just face wash morning and evening. Once that's automatic, add the weekly mask. Build slowly rather than attempting elaborate 10-step routines you'll abandon by day four.

Set phone reminders if needed. Keep products visible near your toothbrush. Habit stacking (face wash right after brushing teeth) makes routines stick.

chunks.heading: Frequently Asked Questions
chunks.content:
If you're still using that bar soap from 2020, it's time. If your girlfriend's face wash is your face wash, it's time. If you can't remember the last time you actually washed your face properly, it's definitely time.

Good skin isn't genetic luck—it's consistent maintenance. The guys who look put-together aren't doing anything complicated. They're just doing the basics correctly and regularly.

How often should I wash my face?

Twice daily—morning and evening. More than that risks over-stripping oils and triggering rebound oil production.

Can I use both charcoal and coffee face wash?

Yes. Alternate based on needs—charcoal for deep clean days, coffee for brightness. Or use charcoal evening, coffee morning.

Will the peel-off mask hurt?

Slight tightness as it dries is normal. Actual pain means you've left it too long. Remove before complete hardening if you have sensitive skin. Avoid areas with facial hair.

How long until I see results?

Immediate: cleaner feeling, reduced oil. One week: fewer breakouts, cleaner pores. Two weeks: noticeably brighter, more even tone. One month: significant improvement in overall skin quality.

Can I use these products if I have acne?

Yes—both face washes help prevent new breakouts. However, if you have severe cystic acne, consult a dermatologist for medical-grade treatments.

Do I need different products for different seasons?

Most men can use the same products year-round. If winter makes your skin unusually dry, add a heavier moisturizer rather than changing cleansers.

What's the right amount of face wash to use?

Nickel to quarter-sized amount. Too little won't clean properly. Too much just wastes product.

Should I use a separate eye makeup remover?

If you don't wear makeup, no. If you do (concealer, etc.), yes—eye area skin is delicate and needs gentler products.

Can women use these products?

Absolutely. Skin is skin. Marketing might be male-focused, but formulas work regardless of gender.

How do I know if a product isn't working for me?

Give it 2-3 weeks. Occasional mild purging (temporary breakouts) is normal as skin adjusts. Persistent irritation, burning, or worsening condition means stop immediately and try something else.

chunks.heading: Your Skin Reflects Your Lifestyle
chunks.content:
Late nights, stress, poor diet, inadequate water intake—all show on your face first. Face wash helps manage symptoms, but addressing root causes matters too.

Drink more water. Sleep better. Manage stress. Eat actual vegetables occasionally. Your skin will respond.

Good skincare isn't complicated. It's just consistency, the right products for your needs, and actually following through instead of buying bottles that sit unused under the sink.

The products exist. The information is here. The only variable left is whether you're ready to stop making excuses and start looking like you have your life together.

blogs.title: Is Charcoal Good For Your Skin?

chunks.heading: What is Activated Charcoal?
chunks.content:
The skincare industry traditionally focused on women’s skin and came out with all types of products to make them look amazing, young and overall presentable. But as the focus shifted to men, researchers worked on the new imperative, which would be more suitable for MEN’S skin. And that’s when we heard about activated charcoal. It’s a close cousin of the charcoal chunks in your barbeque, but has a proven track record of removing toxins and impurities from ANYWHERE. But before we delve into that… let’s first brush up the basics!

List of Content:

1. What is Activated Charcoal?

2. Benefits of Activated Charcoal

3. Benefits of Activated Charcoal in Skincare

4. Is Activated Charcoal Safe?

We referred to ‘close cousins’, but that’s that. Activated Charcoal is NOT like the regular BBQ coal - neither in the way it’s created nor in the way it behaves.

It is both tasteless and odourless and doesn’t react with most things it comes in contact with. It is made in two stages - first, coal and then activated charcoal.

For the first step, a piece of wood is subjected to a very high temperature, close to 1200 degrees. This removes hydrogen, tar and methane from its composition. The coal thus created burns much cleaner than regular charcoal. But we have bigger goals for it than to burn in a petty fireplace.

The second step is the activation stage. Here it is once again subjected to very high temperature, in order to remove all remaining non-carbon substances from inside. This makes the charcoal very porous, increasing its surface area multifold, and gives it a superpower of attraction.

chunks.heading: Benefits of Activated Charcoal in Skincare
chunks.content:
With its newfound superpower, activated charcoal can easily fetch out toxins, chemicals and all types of impurities through a process called adsorption. For those who don’t want to go back to their chemistry class in school, ‘adsorption’ is not a misspelled ‘absorption’. In easy words, it is the process by which things (molecules and ions) stick to the surface of an adsorbing agent (here, charcoal), rather than be absorbed by it. And the best part is that charcoal doesn’t react with any of these, so there’s no fear of unwanted surprises.

Used for Water Treatment. Activated Charcoal has been traditionally used in water treatment plants, so all impurities and chemicals get stuck to the charcoal filters and clean water is passed on. Even the portable water purifiers at home have these charcoal filters to make the water fit for drinking.

Used in Healthcare Facilities. The non-reactive nature of activated charcoal makes it fit to be introduced inside the human body (under strict clinical supervision) for removal of toxins. For example, people with chronic kidney disorders who can’t eliminate waste products like urea as effectively can get rid of them with activated charcoal over a period of time. It is also used in the healthcare system during emergency situations like drug overdose or poisoning, where activated charcoal prevents these toxins from being absorbed by your body and flushes them out with itself.

Activated Charcoal works beautifully as a topical cleansing agent that takes away impurities from the skin and flushes them out with just a splash of water. And it’s very interesting to see how it all works out.

Our skin has millions of pores in it, which collectively act as a permeable sheet to allow things to travel out of the pores (sweat, oil) and also go inside (moisturisers, serums). But among the things that actually make their way inside these pores are dust, pollution, toxins, impurities and PM2.5 particles, which are very harmful - not just for the skin but for your overall health as well. So, when you wash your face, the expectation is that the cleanser will flush all these things out, so that your pores become clean. But most ingredients don’t have a very strong penetration power to reach the spots where these toxins are seated, nor are they trained in binding them on their surface with as much alacrity as we’d wish.

Bang, comes Activated Charcoal - which has 5X penetration and 10X cleansing (adsorption) power, thus going way deeper into the skin and fetching our larger chunks of these toxins. Here’s how different charcoal products can benefit you:

chunks.heading: Is Activated Charcoal Safe?
chunks.content:
Charcoal Face Wash

Charcoal Face Scrub

By going deeper into the pores of the skin and attracting all the toxins and foreign particles on its surface, activated charcoal keeps your skin squeaky clean. This also leads to better skin health and prevents all future skin complications. In short this is the easiest detox for your skin.

Charcoal Face Wash

Charcoal Face Pack

Your skin produces sebum in order to keep itself hydrated and maintain a protective layer on the surface. But too much sebum can clog your pores and cause problems like breakouts and blackheads. Activated charcoal soaks up all the excess oil and clears the pores of dead cells and bacteria to allow your skin to breathe better and stay healthy.

Charcoal Face Wash

Charcoal Sheet Mask

Activated charcoal supports the action of antibacterial agents towards bacterial growth reduction [Source: Antibacterial Agents Adsorbed on Active Carbon: A New Approach for S. aureus and E. coli Pathogen Elimination]. It helps lift acne-causing bacteria from the pores, leaving behind skin that’s unclogged and recovers faster.

Charcoal Pre-Shave Scrub

Charcoal Face Scrub

Charcoal Shaving Foam

Exfoliation is the process of removing dead cells from the surface of your skin, so that it gets free of all deposits and avoid any complication that may arise from such clogging. Activated charcoal excels in attracting impurities like these and particularly works well after skin’s long exposures to pollution and toxins.

First things first, activated charcoal is made of organic substances like coconut shells, bamboo wood, or the likes of the same. And along the process there is no mixing of any external substance in it, so it is pure carbon and nothing else. While carbon can be absorbed by our body in some forms, activated charcoal is absolutely non-reactive and does not affect any natural process going inside the body. Not only does it not get absorbed by the body, it prevents other toxins to be absorbed as well - if administered soon enough.

Similarly, on the surface of the skin, it is one of the safest ingredients to be used for removal of toxins and impurities. But make sure the skincare products you use are free of sulphates and parabens, so that your skin doesn’t have to go through any adverse effects.

chunks.heading: IN SHORT…
chunks.content: Unlike many other ingredients that react with the skin in order to bring about superficial changes in your appearance, activated charcoal is capable of a natural detox. In the process of effective removal of dead skin cells from the pores, it even reduces the appearance of dark spots and balances excessive oil production on the skin while keeping it hydrated.

blogs.title: Should You Use a Moisturizer on Oily Skin?

chunks.heading: What Does a Moisturizer Actually Do?
chunks.content:
If you have grown up believing ‘my skin is already oily, I do not need a cream to make it worse’, then congrats. You have been wrong like many others.

This is one of the most common grooming myths out there, right next to ‘shaving makes your beard grow back thicker.’ It sounds logical, but it is not how skin actually works.

Let’s set the record straight. Oily skin needs a moisturizer. Period.

Here is why.

Your skin can produce excess oil, also known as sebum, and still be dehydrated at the same time. In fact, this is very common. Oil and hydration are not the same thing. Oil is a lipid, while hydration refers to the water content in your skin.

When your skin lacks water, it compensates by producing more oil in an attempt to protect itself and reduce moisture loss. This is why skipping moisturizer often leads to your skin feeling even more greasy over time.

Think of it like this. When you feel like your favorite snacks might run out, you tend to stock up and overbuy. Your skin behaves in a similar way. When it senses a lack of hydration, it increases oil production to make up for it.

So instead of fixing oiliness, skipping moisturizer can actually make it worse.

A good moisturizer does much more than just hydrate. When chosen correctly, it helps your skin function more efficiently and stay balanced.

Here is what a well-formulated moisturizer can do:

- Lock in hydration and reduce water loss

- Support the skin barrier

- Help maintain balanced oil levels over time

- Reduce the chances of irritation and breakouts

In simple terms, it helps your skin stay stable instead of overcompensating.

And no, using a moisturizer will not automatically make your skin greasy. That usually happens when you are using a product that is too heavy or not suited for your skin type.

chunks.heading: Meet the 3-in-1 Moisturizer
chunks.content:
The good thing about today’s skincare science is that there are products specifically designed for oily and acne-prone skin.

If you have oily skin, look for the following:

- Lightweight textures such as gel or water-based formulas

- Products that are less likely to clog pores

- Fast-absorbing formulas that do not leave a heavy residue

- Ingredients that support oil balance and hydration

You will often see certain ingredients mentioned on packaging. Here is what they actually do:

Hyaluronic Acid
Attracts water into the skin, providing hydration without heaviness.

Niacinamide
Regulates sebum production, improves skin texture, and reduces the appearance of pores.

Glycerin
Draws moisture into the skin and helps maintain hydration levels.

Salicylic Acid
Reduces clogging and breakouts.

These ingredients are widely supported by dermatological research and are commonly recommended for oily and acne-prone skin.

Bombay Shaving Company’s 3-in-1 Moisturizer is designed for men who want more than just basic hydration.

It works as a triple action formula that helps control excess oil, support the skin barrier, and improve overall skin clarity in one step.

Powered by Niacinamide, it helps reduce excess oil, improve skin texture, and minimise the appearance of pores, keeping shine under control through the day. At the same time, a Ceramide Complex reinforces the skin’s natural barrier, reduces moisture loss and makes the skin more resilient.

The formula also helps revive dull-looking skin by improving overall clarity and supporting a more even-looking tone, so your skin appears fresher and healthier.

All of this comes in a lightweight, non-sticky, fast-absorbing texture that works well across seasons, from dry winters to humid days.

It is also compact and travel friendly, making it easy to carry whether you are heading to college, the office, or out for the evening.

chunks.heading: Signs You Are Doing It Right
chunks.content:
No complicated routines. Just the basics done right.

Step 1: Cleanser
Use a gentle face wash, ideally gel or foam based. Look for ingredients like Salicylic Acid, Tea Tree, or Charcoal.
Wash your face with lukewarm water to remove excess oil and reduce the risk of clogged pores.
Avoid overly harsh cleansers, as they can strip natural oils and disrupt the skin barrier.
You can try something like the Anti Acne Face Wash.

Step 2: Toner
Choose an alcohol-free toner with ingredients like Niacinamide or mild exfoliants.
Apply it after cleansing to help remove leftover residue and improve skin texture.

Step 3: Moisturizer
Use a lightweight, oil-free, gel-based moisturizer, or opt for a 3-in-1 moisturizer and apply it evenly on skin
Skipping this step can lead to increased oil production over time.

Step 4: Sunscreen
Apply sunscreen after moisturizing.
This helps protect your skin from tanning, sun damage, and premature aging.
A good option is the Aloe Vera Sunscreen Gel.

- Don’t forget to wash your face at night to remove dirt, oil, and pollution collected throughout the day.

- Use a moisturizer at night as well, either the same one or a slightly more hydrating option

- Exfoliate one to two times a week to prevent buildup. You can use the Coffee Face Scrub.

- Avoid harsh soaps and aggressive scrubbing

- Do not wash your face excessively

- Stay consistent with your routine

Once you start using the right moisturizer consistently, you will notice:

- Your skin looks balanced instead of overly shiny

- A less greasy T-zone

- Fewer breakouts

- Pores that appear less visible

- Skin that looks fresh and healthy instead of tired

chunks.heading: In Conclusion…
chunks.content:
Not using a moisturizer can be just as problematic as using the wrong one.

Oily skin is not the enemy. Unbalanced and dehydrated skin is.

Instead of trying to strip your skin of oil, focus on giving it what it actually needs:

- Hydration

- Balance

- Consistent care

- The right products

Think of it like ordering a full meal and leaving halfway through. You’re going to stay hungry and be with half the nourishment.

Cleansing your face without following it up with a moisturizer can disrupt your skin’s balance. If you do not restore hydration, your skin may compensate by producing more oil.

So skipping moisturizer is not solving oiliness. It is quietly making it worse.

blogs.title: Soap vs Face Wash vs Face Scrub: What’s the Real Difference?

chunks.heading: What does it do?
chunks.content:
You’ve just walked into your bathroom, ready to get rid of all the dirt and oil you’ve collected over the last few hours.

You splash some water on your face and look up to see three products on your sink fighting for your attention:

- Your go-to soap bar.

- A handy face wash.

- And a powerful face scrub.

Which one are you choosing for your precious face?

Let us help you out.

Your face has thinner, more sensitive skin. It also produces more oil than the rest of your body. Every day, it deals with pollution, sweat, sunscreen, and stress.

So when you hit it with harsh products, or no products at all, your face will definitely retaliate, and you’ll see the outcome sooner than you think.

Always remember - grooming and personal care isn’t about doing more or buying more products. It’s about doing things right.

Now, let’s meet the three main characters.

Soap is the oldest, simplest cleanser, something we’ve all used since childhood. It’s made to remove dirt, oil, and bacteria from your skin. Great for your body. Solid for hands. But… risky for your face.

Soap works by breaking down oils and washing them away. Sounds helpful, right? Except it does not know when to stop.

It removes:

- Dirt

- Sweat

- Excess oil

- And… your skin’s natural barrier

That barrier keeps your skin smooth, balanced, and calm. When soap strips it away, your face becomes vulnerable.

With daily use, your skin can start feeling dry, tight, flaky, irritated, oilier, and more prone to breakouts.

Simply put, soap aggressively removes oil from your skin. Your skin gets confused and starts overproducing it to compensate. That’s how you end up with both dry and greasy skin at the same time.

chunks.heading: What does it do?
chunks.content:
- In emergency situations when nothing else is around

- After being in a place with heavy dirt or sweat (once in a while)

- If the soap is specifically made for your face

But as a daily face cleanser? Soap is not the right choice for you.

Face wash is smart cleaning. It’s designed specifically for facial skin, which means it cleans without destroying your moisture barrier.

It removes:

- Dirt

- Oil

- Pollution

- Sweat

- Sunscreen

All while keeping your skin’s natural moisture intact.

What’s better, there are multiple options for every skin type. Whether you have oily skin, sensitive skin, or combination skin, there’s something for everyone.

Using a face wash daily helps maintain natural oils, prevents breakouts, feels fresh (not tight), and preps your skin for shaving.

Think of face wash like brushing your teeth, but for your face. You don’t skip it, and you don’t overdo it.

If you only pick one product from this list, Daily De-Tan Face Wash is non-negotiable.

We know what you’re thinking: if a face wash already handles daily cleaning, what’s the point of a face scrub?

Simply put, a face scrub isn’t meant to clean, it’s meant to exfoliate and renew.

Unlike face washes, scrubs contain tiny particles (or chemical exfoliants) that remove dead skin cells from the surface.

It helps to:

- Unclog pores

- Remove dead skin

- Smooth texture

- Boost glow

- Prevent ingrown hairs

Basically, it clears away old skin and reveals a fresher layer underneath.

But here’s the catch - scrubs are powerful. And with great power comes great responsibility.

Using a scrub daily or over-scrubbing your face can lead to redness, sensitivity, micro-tears, breakouts, and dry patches.

chunks.heading: Final take: Clean smart, not hard
chunks.content:
- 2–3 times a week

- Before shaving for smoother results

- At night, when your skin can recover

Always use it gently. Let the scrub do the work.

- Soap - Basic cleaner, harsh for the face

- Face Wash - Daily cleanser, gentle and effective

- Face Scrub - Exfoliator, removes dead skin

All different. All useful. None interchangeable.

- Use a Daily De-Tan Face Wash daily, morning and night

- Use a Coffee Face Scrub 2–3 times a week

- Use soap - never

That’s it. No 12-step ritual. No drama.

Your face isn’t asking for luxury. It’s asking for logic.

So stop playing roulette with your skin and build a routine that actually works:

- Wash daily

- Scrub weekly

- Don’t treat your face like the rest of your body

That’s it! That’s all you need to do!

blogs.title: 5 Things to do to Surprise Your Partner this Valentine's Day

chunks.heading: A "Couple's Activities" Gift Basket
chunks.content:
Valentine's Day is just around the corner, and if you're looking for a way to surprise the special man in your life with a Valentine’s day gift, you've come to the right place! First things first, let's talk about what not to do. Don't just give him a boring gift like a new tie or a box of chocolates. Those gifts are too predictable and show that you haven’t put much thought into it.

Instead, think outside the box and get creative! Easier said than done, right? Well, you’re in luck because we’ve already picked our brains on this and here’s a ready-made DIY list of things that you can do, depending on what kind of chemistry and interests the two of you share. Read on for quirky gift ideas that are sure to surprise and delight your partner on Valentine's Day that also double up as the perfect activities that you can do together to celebrate your love.

Spice things up and create lasting memories together with an adventure for two. Start by gathering a basket and fill it with all essentials for an exciting day out. This could include a picnic blanket, a sunscreen lotion, matching water bottles and some easy snacks like sandwiches. Thanks to the weather around Valentine’s Day the sweet outdoors will allow you a good time both in the sun and under the shade of a tree. So, take a hike, go on a biking trail or simply go sit in the park and play fun games for two…

Wondering what games to play with your husband or boyfriend this Valentine's Day? Here’s our top 10 list:

1. Two Truths and a Lie: Take turns sharing three statements about yourself, with one of them being a lie. Your partner must try to guess which statement is the lie.

2. Would You Rather: Take turns asking each other hypothetical "Would You Rather" questions, such as "Would you rather travel to the past or the future?" or "Would you rather have a million dollars or true love?"

3. The Question Game: One person starts by asking a question, any question, and then the next person must answer it and come up with a question of their own. This can be a fun way to learn more about each other and have some interesting conversations.

4. Never Have I Ever: Take turns making statements starting with "Never have I ever...", such as "Never have I ever skydived." Anyone who has done the thing mentioned must put a finger down. The one who loses all their fingers first, loses the game.

5. The Story Game: One person starts a story with a few sentences and then the other person continues it. The story can be fiction or non-fiction, but it should be something that both people are interested in.

chunks.heading: A "Memory Lane" Gift
chunks.content:
6. The Name Game: One person thinks of a celebrity or fictional character, and then the other person must ask yes or no questions to figure out who it is.

7. The Word Association Game: One person says a word and the next person must say the first word that comes to mind. The game continues until one person can't think of a word.

8. The Debate Game: Choose a topic you both are passionate about and debate the pros and cons. The goal is to convince the other person to see your point of view.

9. The Memory Game: One person says a word, and then the next person must say a word that's associated with the previous word. The game continues until one person can't think of a word.

10. The Drawing Game: One person draws a picture or a simple shape and the next person must add to the drawing. The goal is to see how the drawing evolves and to have fun with it.

Creating a memory-lane Gift for Your Husband /boyfriend is a thoughtful and sentimental way to show him how much you care. But what’s even more special is to do it together, so that not just you but the both of you reminisce about your past together and celebrate your love for each other. Here’s what you gotta do…

Step 1: Gather mementos and memories from your past together

These could be anything from photographs, love letters, or even small trinkets that hold special meaning. Look through your old albums (both physical and digital), scrapbooks, and keepsake boxes to find items that you can include in your gift.

Step 2: Create a Theme For Your Gift

You could make a timeline of your relationship, showcasing the different milestones and memories that you’ve shared together or create a memory scrapbook with pictures and souvenirs from special trips or occasions.

Step 3: Build and Personalise Your Gift

Use a wooden box and put your respective mementos/memories into the box that you’ve gathered. Alternatively, create a photo album or a memory wall in your house with a collage of your memories together. This could be a great way to create a focal point in your bedroom or living room.

chunks.heading: A "Couple’s DIY Skincare" Gift
chunks.content:
Having a DIY skincare day at home with your husband/boyfriend can be a fun and relaxing way to spend time together on Valentine's Day, while also taking care of your skin. Just follow the steps and have fun:

Step 1: Plan Ahead

Before you begin, make sure to plan ahead and gather all the materials and ingredients you will need. This could include things like facial kits, herbs and fruits. You can either find recipes and tutorials online or simply order one online to save time and focus on the activity instead.
